We introduce a 3D latent-action world model that learns continuous action representations directly from point-cloud observations of retargeted human manipulation demonstrations. A contrastive objective is used to encourage consistent representations of motion across embodiments. The resulting unified latent action space serves directly as the search space for model-predictive control, where sampled latent actions condition particle-based future predictions. Executable robot commands are then recovered from the predicted geometric motion without requiring an embodiment-specific action decoder. Through extensive evaluations, we demonstrate that the learned latent actions exhibit controllable and compositional motion, transfer to unseen robot embodiments, and support zero-shot manipulation with unseen gripper geometries. Following task-agnostic adaptation, our model achieves 90%, 92%, and 60% success on reaching, grasping, and placing, respectively, compared with DexWM's reported 72%, 58%, and 28%. Finally, we demonstrate zero-shot real-world manipulation with an unseen dexterous hand, achieving an 86% success rate across 50 trials on five diverse tasks involving pushing, grasping, and lifting everyday objects. These results highlight the potential of geometry-grounded latent actions as a unified, transferable interface for world-model-based robotic manipulation. Project materials, including demonstration videos and source code, are available at https://vinaymohan0409.github.io/DexLatentWorld/.

title: Probing radial flow via the differential flow coefficient $v_0(p_T)$ using CMS open data
summary: We present a comprehensive study of the differential radial flow coefficient $v_0(p_T)$ and its $p_T$-integrated counterpart $v_0$ in Pb+Pb collisions at $\sqrt{s_{NN}} = 2.76~\mathrm{TeV}$, using CMS open data for mid-peripheral centrality classes of 50--60\% and 60--70\%. The measured $v_0(p_T)$ distributions are compared with ATLAS measurements at $\sqrt{s_{NN}} = 5.02~\mathrm{TeV}$, revealing a clear energy dependence in the overall magnitude of radial flow fluctuations. Notably, the scaled ratio $v_0(p_T)/v_0$ exhibits an approximate universality that is largely independent of both collision energy and centrality at low $p_T$, persisting up to $p_T\sim3~\mathrm{GeV}$, suggesting that the integrated $v_0$ encodes most of the energy-dependent information. We compare the data with the \textsc{Jetscape} multi-stage hybrid model, using Gaussian process emulators trained on a principal component analysis of the model output to explore the full 17-dimensional parameter space. A global variance-based sensitivity analysis using Sobol indices shows that, for the Grad viscous correction, the nucleon fluctuation parameter $σ_k$ is the dominant source of variance for $v_0$, $v_0(p_T)$, and $v_0(p_T)/v_0$, followed by the free-streaming parameters $τ_R$ and $α$ and the nucleon width $w$. The sensitivity to the bulk viscosity peak $(ζ/s)_{\max}$ is weak for $v_0$ but increases for $v_0(p_T)$ and for the scaled ratio. Emulator predictions, calibrated on $p_T$-integrated observables and on scaled spectra, describe the data reasonably well at low and intermediate $p_T$. Parameters calibrated at $\sqrt{s_{NN}} = 2.76~\mathrm{TeV}$ also describe the ATLAS $v_0(p_T)/v_0$ data at $5.02~\mathrm{TeV}$, supporting a near universal momentum dependence of radial flow fluctuations across collision energies.

title: GlanceNav: Efficient Vision-and-Language Navigation with Streaming Memory and Counterfactual Rewind
summary: Multimodal large language models (MLLMs) have become strong policies for vision-and-language navigation (VLN). However, most of them encode a sample of past frames again at every decision and are trained on isolated decisions, so computation is redundant and the usable history is short. They also learn from their own mistakes through outcome rewards that give one scalar to a whole episode. We ask whether a navigator can encode each frame only once, at a constant cost per step, and still remember what matters and learn efficiently from its mistakes. We present GlanceNav, a streaming navigator built on a hybrid MLLM. Its Gated DeltaNet layers carry a recurrent state through the whole episode, while its attention layers keep a short window of recent observations and a small bank of keyframes, selected by how much each frame changes the recurrent state. This constant-size memory keeps the cost per step fixed and allows training on whole episodes with the same memory as at inference. Because the entire memory can also be copied in constant time, we further propose Counterfactual Rewind (CoRe), a reinforcement learning stage that rewinds a drifting rollout to its closest approach to the goal, lets an expert correct a few actions, and credits decisions by the resulting change in outcome. Trained only on the R2R-CE and RxR-CE training splits, with 1,000 instructions for reinforcement learning, a 4B GlanceNav reaches success rates of 71.9% and 73.6% on R2R-CE and RxR-CE val-unseen. On R2R-CE, it outperforms the strongest previous single-RGB method trained without external data by 9.1 points, while running at 104 ms per step.

title: World Models as Native Latent Action Models
summary: Large and diverse video sources, such as egocentric human video and heterogeneous robot recordings, carry rich dynamics but come either without actions or without a shared action space. Latent action models (LAMs) can recover these dynamics, but they train their inverse- and forward-dynamics models (IDM, FDM) from scratch, trading off pixel reconstruction against latent capacity and accuracy. Pretrained video world models natively generate high-fidelity dynamics, yet represent them densely, entangled across all layers. Viewing the world model as a LAM, we show that these dynamics can be extracted with minimal changes to the model. Native LAM operates one pretrained video diffusion transformer as both IDM and FDM, with learnable dynamics registers as the only causal bridge between the two, and trains on counterfactual temporal pairs that differ in motion alone, so that the registers distill a video's dynamics into a compact native latent action. We further propose a pretraining paradigm for vision-language-action (VLA) policies, Pretraining Actions from World models (PAWlicy), in which Native LAM serves as a dynamics teacher on large-scale video; unlike world action models, it never generates video. Native latent actions outperform existing LAMs on the LARY benchmark in both action classification and control regression, and replay the same motion on new robots, in new scenes, and from human hands to robots, although no transfer objective is used in training. With a 3.8B model, PAWlicy reaches a 93.6% average success rate on RoboTwin 2.0 trained with domain-randomized demonstrations, the highest among VLAs. On RoboDojo, it is competitive on every dimension we evaluate, and its Precision, evaluated by us, is on par with the leading leaderboard entries. On real robots, it improves over the pi_0.5 baseline on both tasks. Both stages use only public data and a publicly released world model.

title: Useful but Unwieldy: How Software Engineers Perceive the Design of Chain-of-Thought Explanations in Coding Agents
summary: Coding agents (CAs) powered by Large Language Models (LLMs) are increasingly integrated into software engineering (SE) workflows. As these CAs take up more tasks and responsibilities, it is imperative for software engineers to understand the CA's rationale behind its' decisions, also known as the chain-of-thought (CoT). During the interaction, some CAs are capable of showing this CoT as a separate message to users with the goal of providing transparency and explainability. However, its effectiveness as an explainable AI (XAI) mechanism for end-users in software engineering has not yet been established in the literature. This motivates us to understand their experiences with the CoT message as an XAI tool through a survey and semi-structured follow-up interviews with 36 software engineers. Through thematic analysis of the survey responses and interview transcripts, we found that CoT message is an indispensable tool for software engineers in terms of transparency, scrutability, and trust towards the CA. However, various instances of CoT messages being overly verbose, containing technical information that does not match the users' expertise, or being perceived by the users as ``detached'' from the conversation because the ``agent is talking to itself'', lead to comprehension difficulties and selective use or abandonment of the tool. We synthesize these insights to inform the design of CoT messages that support software engineers in their explainability needs.

title: AeroJEPA: A Two-Stage Framework for Aerosol Forecasting with Joint-Embedding Predictive Learning
summary: Aerosol forecasting requires integrating sparse ground observations and modeling meteorologically driven concentration evolution and spatial structure. However, analysis-initialized forecasts make limited explicit use of historical observations, while pointwise regression tends to smooth local variations and provides limited constraints on fine spatial structures. In this work, we propose AeroJEPA, a two-stage joint-embedding predictive framework for regional surface PM$_{2.5}$ forecasting. Specifically, Stage I fuses historical observations, model backgrounds, and meteorological information to predict an initial future state, meteorological conditions, and multi-scale structures. Morphology-guided encoding and joint-embedding predictive supervision support learning future spatial representations, supplementing concentration regression with structural constraints. Stage II uses predicted meteorology to guide state refinement and incorporates coarse- and fine-scale structures into state updates and decoding to generate the concentration field at a single future time step. Experiments show that AeroJEPA reduces gridded and independent-station RMSE by 17.23\% and 7.90\%, respectively, relative to PFGNet, while improving spatial consistency with analysis fields. In a 48 h recursive forecasting case study, AeroJEPA generally achieves lower RMSE and MAE than the numerical forecasts across the forecast period, indicating promising short- to medium-range forecasting performance.

title: Tabular Foundation Models Are Surprisingly Effective In-Context Robot Learners
summary: Can foundation models pretrained for generic numerical prediction serve as in-context robot learners? We investigate this question through tabular foundation models (TFMs), which are pretrained to infer input-output relationships from labeled examples in context. We introduce TabAct, which casts visual imitation as numerical prediction: frozen visual features and robot proprioception form the inputs, future action chunks form the targets, and each demonstration time step provides one labeled example that conditions a frozen TFM for closed-loop control. The predictor receives no robot-specific training or target-task fine-tuning. With one target-task demonstration available to each method, TabAct with TabICLv2 achieves the highest average success among all evaluated methods on both LIBERO and Meta-World, exceeding the strongest baseline by 20.9 and 5.8 percentage points, respectively. Additional demonstrations improve control without updating model weights: with five demonstrations, success reaches 94.2% on LIBERO-Object. These results demonstrate that generic numerical pretraining can provide an effective foundation for in-context robot learning.

title: A High-Resolution UAV Benchmark Dataset and Baseline Evaluation for Teak Crown Segmentation in Western Ghats Tropical Forests
summary: Accurate teak-tree segmentation from high-resolution drone imagery is critical for sustainable plantation management, yet lacks dedicated benchmarks. We introduce TeakTreeNet, a comprehensive dataset and evaluation protocol for binary teak-tree segmentation at native 2cm resolution. Four state-of-the-art architectures: U-Net, PSPNet, DeepLabV3, and SegFormer were rigorously benchmarked across scratch and ImageNet-pretrained settings with three-seed reproducibility. SegFormer establishes new SOTA performance with F1 0.938 +/- 0.002 (Teak), IoU 0.968 +/- 0.001 (Teak), and Accuracy 0.986 +/- 0.001, outperforming all pretrained CNNs. Domain-adaptive training suffices, as the scratch SegFormer outperforms ImageNet pretrained baselines, avoiding large-scale pretraining overhead. Comprehensive analysis reveals Transformer's superior boundary delineation for dense plantation scenarios. TeakTreeNet provides researchers with 6391 expertly annotated drone patches (224x224) and establishes reproducible evaluation protocols, enabling direct comparison of future methods. Our benchmark demonstrates SegFormer's optimal balance of accuracy, efficiency, and deployability for operational forestry monitoring of teak plantations for India's western tropical forests.

title: AnchorCredit: Output-Anchored Credit Assignment for Structured Generation with Multiple Verifiable Rewards
summary: In Reinforcement Learning with Verifiable Rewards (RLVR), Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO) and related methods typically compute group-relative advantages from response rewards and broadcast the same advantage to every generated token in a response to guide policy updates. However, we identify a systematic problem of cross-component credit misassignment in tasks with multiple verifiable results, such as joint multi-attribute prediction: low rewards for some components can penalize a well-performing component and its associated reasoning. To address this problem, we propose AnchorCredit. The method uses the policy model's attention from output anchors to preceding reasoning sentences to estimate sentence-component associations and assign component-specific advantages to the relevant reasoning, without additional relevance annotations or a separate relevance discriminator. To support the study of credit assignment with multiple verifiable rewards, we construct ProductAttr, a benchmark of 7,200 real product image-text samples. Experiments show that AnchorCredit outperforms existing baselines on this benchmark. Experiments on the public Nutrition5k dataset further support the method's effectiveness in this setting.

title: Learning the Next Best Move with Visual Diffusion Models
summary:
In this paper, we show that visual diffusion models can learn to predict the next best move (NBM) in tasks requiring sequential reasoning and lookahead, without explicitly exploring future steps or exhaustive searching at inference. Previous work demonstrated that these models can generate complete solutions to geometric and reasoning problems. Here, we show that simple fine-tuning on visual state--NBM pairs enables a pretrained model to select actions whose value depends on consequences several steps ahead. Each move is predicted directly in image space from the current state, without an explicit symbolic representation or search procedure. Repeated NBM predictions then construct a solution one decision at a time.
  We demonstrate this capability on chess puzzles and tile-based pathfinding, and show that it extends to Connect Four, Go and billiards. In chess, the model predicts legal moves and finds the best move far more often than by recalling similar training positions, including piece sacrifices whose benefit emerges only through later tactical continuations. In pathfinding, it constructs shortest paths on uniform-cost maps and cost-optimal routes across terrain tiles with different traversal costs, choosing longer routes when they are cheaper overall. These costs are learned implicitly from examples, without numerical cost supervision. These results show that direct visual move prediction can support globally informed decisions and successful sequential problem solving.

title: Semantic-aware Decoding for Diverse Text-to-SQL under Schema Ambiguity
summary: Real-world text-to-SQL systems often face schema ambiguity, where a question can map to multiple plausible schema elements. To support downstream disambiguation, SQL generation systems should include diverse interpretations among their top-k predictions. However, large language models (LLMs) typically favor a single interpretation, producing highly skewed outputs. We propose Semantic-aware Logit Adjustment (SLA), a training-free decoding method that promotes diverse SQL generation by adjusting token logits based on semantic similarity between schema elements. Unlike prior approaches that rely on reasoning-intensive prompting or task-specific fine-tuning, SLA is efficient, model-agnostic, and easy to deploy. Experiments show that SLA consistently improves interpretation coverage over standard decoding and remains competitive with existing diversity-oriented methods at substantially lower inference cost.

title: Joint Flow-Matching Posteriors for Overlapping LISA Galactic Binaries
summary: Laser Interferometer Space Antenna (LISA) will observe millions of galactic binaries (GBs) at once, thousands of them resolvable, with signals that overlap in frequency. Separating them requires a global fit, a joint inference of all sources, which today takes Markov chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) samplers hours to days on a cluster and is repeated for each new stretch of data. We adapt recent advances in large-scale diffusion models, flow matching with a multimodal transformer, to learn the joint posterior once and then draw from it in a fraction of a second. We evaluate our approach on a realistic simulator, with full instrument response and noise, priors fitted to a simulated Galactic catalogue, and sources sampled anywhere in the entire 0.1 to 16 mHz frequency band. We demonstrate that the approach is scalable to up to 15 653 sources fitted simultaneously, evaluating calibration and coverage w.r.t. the MCMC baseline. The results show that this approach could be realistically scaled to tackle the full global fit problem.

title: MUNDO: a multiresolution generative framework for temporal downscaling
summary: Dynamical systems are often observed at coarse temporal resolution through sparse states or temporal aggregates, leaving the underlying fine-scale trajectories unresolved. Recovering these trajectories requires probabilistic models that capture the unresolved variability while remaining consistent with the observations. We present MUNDO (Multiresolution UNified DOwnscaling), a generative framework for temporal downscaling under general linear observation operators. MUNDO introduces a null-space parameterization that enforces exact observation consistency in a single network evaluation, unifying temporal interpolation and disaggregation. To capture complex multiscale dynamics, we leverage reverse Markov learning to factorize the observation operator into a hierarchy of successive coarsenings. Each level models only the degrees of freedom lost between adjacent resolutions. We evaluate MUNDO on two-scale Lorenz-96, four two-dimensional physical systems, and multivariate ERA5 reanalysis over Europe, for both temporal interpolation and disaggregation. Across datasets and tasks, MUNDO generally outperforms flow-based baselines. Single-step MUNDO achieves strong predictive skill, while recursive MUNDO generally improves temporal realism and ensemble calibration, with better spread-skill agreement and predictive coverage.

title: RenGen: Generating Images with as Many Tokens as the Scene Needs
summary: We present RenGen, a latent diffusion model that generates simple scenes from a few tokens and busy scenes from many, saving time and compute on simple scenes without losing realism. Most latent generators represent every image as a fixed grid of patch tokens, so a simple image costs as much to generate as a complex one. Prior methods that vary the token count through content-adaptive tokenization lose image quality as the count shrinks. RenGen instead trades scene complexity, rather than image quality, for fewer tokens. It does so by generating in the latent space of a pretrained region encoder, where each token represents one region of the image, and a decoder renders these region tokens back into pixels. Unlike patch tokens, region tokens cover areas of varying shape and position, so each token must capture both what its region contains and where it lies on the image canvas. We encode this spatial extent by adding positional embeddings to the encoder features before pooling, and we generate it by anchoring each token to a single randomly sampled point, from which the generator infers the region's shape, size, and content. At sampling time, the number of anchor points sets the trade-off between scene complexity and compute. On ImageNet $256{\times}256$, RenGen reaches a gFID of 1.34 with 88 tokens per image on average, the best among methods that vary their token count. It approaches the quality of RAEv2, a state-of-the-art patch-based model, at $2.5{\times}$ lower latency, advancing the Pareto frontier of generation quality versus compute. RenGen's gFID stays flat across scene complexity while latency varies by $2.4{\times}$ between simplest and busiest scenes, and its autoencoder reconstructs nearly as well as RAEv2 (rFID 0.32 vs. 0.30) with $2.9{\times}$ fewer tokens.

title: Early Realignment of Eccentric Planetary Orbits without Orbital Decay
summary: Warm Jupiters are, on average, more closely aligned with their host stars than hot Jupiters, even at high eccentricities. The low projected obliquities of eccentric warm Jupiters on the tidal migration track are difficult to reconcile with high-eccentricity migration (HEM) pathways that excite large misalignments. We examine whether tides acting on the star can realign initially misaligned systems before their orbits circularize. We extend a frequency-dependent tidal model to arbitrary eccentricities and focus on the $(1,0)$ obliquity tide. This component is stationary in the inertial frame, dissipates stellar rotational energy, and can change spin obliquity while leaving the semimajor axis and eccentricity unchanged. Its forcing frequency in the stellar rotating frame coincides with that of the rigid spin-over mode, which is non-dissipative. The strength of dissipation by non-rigid motions at this same frequency remains uncertain. In our models, enhancing the dissipative response by a factor of $10^7$ produces appreciable obliquity damping for Jupiter-mass planets. The stronger damping for more massive planets suggests that an enhancement of $10^6$ may suffice for super-Jupiters. Realignment can outpace circularization if the planet is already on an eccentric warm orbit while the star is still inflated and rapidly rotating during the pre-main sequence (PMS). If alignment occurs then, present-day stellar effective temperature may be a weak predictor of obliquity. In binary-driven HEM runs initialized at the zero-age main sequence, orbital circularization outpaces realignment in systems with sustained eccentricity forcing. The stellar quadrupole scaling suggests substantially stronger suppression of eccentricity excitation for PMS starts. These results cast doubt on binary-driven HEM as the origin of such aligned eccentric warm Jupiters, even when they lie along the tidal migration track.

title: SYCLDB: A Cross-Vendor Heterogeneous Analytical DBMS
summary: The rapid growth of AI and analytical workloads has increased the need for fast, interactive analytical data processing. This, in turn, has led to a surge of interest in designing accelerated analytical database engines that can exploit modern GPUs to scale computation. While GPUs provide the massive data-parallelism required by modern analytics, the software landscape remains dominated by closed-source, vendor-locked programming models, like CUDA, limiting portability across multi-vendor GPUs. In this work, we present SYCLDB, an end-to-end analytical database engine built upon the SYCL open standard, designed to enable efficient, hardware-agnostic execution across a wide range of accelerators using a single codebase. By implementing core relational operators as modular SYCL kernels, integrating them with a SQL frontend based on Apache Calcite and Apache Thrift, and supporting Apache Arrow for efficient columnar ingestion, SYCLDB reduces dependence on vendor-specific GPU programming stacks by enabling a single SYCL codebase to execute analytical query pipelines across Intel, AMD, and NVIDIA GPUs.

title: Analytic $k$-essence Inflation
summary: In this work we develop a fully analytic $k$-essence inflation solution which is compatible with the observational constraints on inflation, without the need for the slow-roll assumption being imposed dynamically in the field equations. The analytic solution is obtained for a kinetic scalar sector of the form $K(X)= \frac{X^n}{X_s^{n-1}}$ and for the scalar field satisfying a tracking condition $\dotφ^2=γH^{-m}$. For this class of theories, the sound speed of the primordial curvature perturbations is constant, so no gradient instabilities occur in the theory. The Hubble rate, the scale factor and the scalar field can be analytically expressed as functions of the cosmic time, and the observational indices of inflation depend solely on the parameters $n$ and $m$. The resulting evolution is inflationary and it develops a pressure singularity a few $e$-foldings after the end of inflation. However, using qualitative and quantitative numerical arguments, we show that the pressure singularity is classically avoided when the matter fluids of radiation and cold dark matter are taken into account.

title: Quantifying and calibrating precision gain from covariate adjustment in clinical trials with binary endpoints
summary: Covariate adjustment is widely used in randomized clinical trials to improve estimation and inference of treatment effects. For continuous endpoints, the reasoning is straightforward: prognostic baseline covariates explain outcome variability and thereby increase precision. For binary endpoints, however, the situation is more complex because conditional and marginal effects generally differ in nonlinear outcome models such as logistic regression. We develop a theoretical framework for quantifying the maximum attainable first-order precision gain from covariate adjustment when estimating marginal treatment effects for binary endpoints. We derive a closed-form identity showing that precision-gain potential is governed by an estimand- and allocation-specific combination of the treatment-specific risk functions. Building on this identity, we introduce marginal prognostic strength as a population-level measure of prognostic information and characterize when it determines precision-gain potential and when the two quantities decouple. Specifically, substantial prognostic information within both treatment arms need not translate into improved precision for the marginal treatment effect when covariates are predictive on the target effect scale. We further develop a calibration algorithm for methodological simulation studies that preserves prespecified conditional outcome structures and marginal risks while allowing data-generating mechanisms to be calibrated by marginal prognostic strength and evaluated in terms of estimand-specific precision-gain potential. Together, these results provide a theoretical and practical framework for understanding, quantifying, and calibrating potential precision gains from covariate adjustment for binary endpoints.

title: DyLoMo-DiT: Dynamic Looped Mixture-of-Experts Diffusion Transformers
summary: Diffusion Transformers (DiTs) scale model capacity by increasing both parameter count and computation. Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) variants expand parameter capacity while keeping per-token computation roughly fixed, but still require substantial parameter storage. In this paper, we propose Dynamic Looped MoE DiT (DyLoMo-DiT), which reuses parameters rather than adding them: a weight-shared loop repeatedly applies the middle layers, while sparse experts allocate parameter capacity across tokens. This design deepens the network without adding parameters, freeing the parameter budget for other uses, such as more experts or more distinct layers. It also allocates compute dynamically, varying the number of passes across noise levels. Experiments show that DyLoMo-DiT makes more effective use of parameter and compute budgets, with further gains from assigning more passes to low-noise steps. On ImageNet $256\times256$, DyLoMo-DiT reduces FID by 11-24% relative to DiT and 36-56% relative to DiT-MoE at matched parameter and compute budgets. For text-to-image generation, a scaled DyLoMo-DiT achieves a higher GenEval score than FLUX.1 (0.714 vs. 0.673), with less than one tenth of its active parameters (1.05B vs. 12B).

title: Certified Defense against Adversarial Patches on Traffic Signs via Mask-Aware Training
summary: Adversarial patches are a practical threat to traffic-sign recognition: a small sticker on a sign can change a classifier's decision. PatchCleanser is a certified defense that applies two rounds of masking and, for every image it certifies, provably returns the correct label for any patch that fits inside one mask. We show that on traffic signs the defense certifies almost nothing when paired with a normally trained classifier (1.7% to 4.8% certified accuracy on GTSRB), because a single mask can hide the small central symbol that distinguishes sign classes. We propose mask-aware training, which trains the classifier on images occluded by random pairs drawn from the defense's own mask set, with a sampling bias toward masks over the sign's centre. The defense, mask set and certification procedure are unchanged, so the guarantee is preserved. For an ImageNet-pretrained ResNet-50, mask-aware training raises certified accuracy from 4.8% to 60.0%. Under real per-image adversarial patches, the defended ResNet-50 reaches 85.7% accuracy, versus 74.6% for the original PatchCleanser with a normally trained ResNet-50.

title: SARA: An Auditor-in-the-Loop LLM Recommender for Sustainability Reports
summary: Auditing corporate sustainability reports requires assurance professionals to map a company-specific checklist drawn from roughly 1,700 regulatory requirements onto the relevant passages of lengthy, repeatedly revised draft reports and to judge compliance. We present SARA (Sustainability Reporting Assistant), a human-in-the-loop recommender system delivered as a Microsoft Word add-in that recommends, for each requirement, the passages addressing it and predicts a compliance verdict while keeping the auditor in full control. SARA casts auditing as content-based recommendation over a fixed regulatory taxonomy and makes per-requirement large language model (LLM) matching cheaper, faster, and more accurate through topic-prediction filtering: on expert-annotated reports, it reduces matching cost about sixfold and runtime by 42% versus feeding the full report to the LLM. It is in production use across PwC Germany's sustainability-assurance practice.

title: Turbulent Epidemics: Scale-dependent Fluctuations as a Probe of Population Heterogeneity
summary: Heterogeneous dynamics, including phenomena such as superspreading and clustering, is a hallmark of many infectious diseases. A key challenge lies in identifying observables that constrain heterogeneous dynamics. We here adapt the technique of turbulence decomposition from fluid dynamics to extract scale-dependent fluctuation spectra and correlation functions from disaggregated epidemiological data as a probe of population heterogeneity. To investigate possible explanations for the observed heterogeneities during the COVID-19 winter wave in Germany in 2020/21, we calculate synthetic observables using the new network-based simulation code \textsc{Epimetheus} for an idealized structured population. The code can flexibly incorporate clustering, heterogeneous connectivity and susceptibility, superspreading as well as temporal modulations of transmission risk and factors like waning of immunity and vaccination. A qualitative comparison of simulated and observed fluctuation spectra and correlation functions as well as the secondary attack rate and the overdispersion indicates that both clustering and variations of susceptibility across population substructures of all scales are required to produce the observed dynamics. Combined with heterogeneous connectivity, it is likely that self-limiting effects would have limited the winter outbreak to $0.2\texttt{-}0.35$ of the population without further behavioral changes after the autumn of 2020. A uniform population-wide reduction of transmission risk alone does not adequately explain the observed heterogeneities. Further analysis of the relative contributions and interplay of interventions and self-limiting effects on COVID-19 disease dynamics is required. We outline avenues towards a better integration of heterogeneity in models for predicting infectious disease dynamics and diagnosing effects of interventions.

title: The KL Divergence Is Never Negative, Except in PyTorch
summary: A Kullback--Leibler (KL) divergence is never negative, yet PyTorch users have reported negative values for years, and the standard advice is to clamp them at zero. The sign is only the visible part of a silent failure. Many machine-learning applications compare nearby distributions, where conventional KL formulas lose accuracy. On 8.5 million inputs with certified references across 18 closed-form KL families and F.kl_div, we find widespread errors in values and gradients on CPU and GPU. Among scalar families in ordinary parameter ranges, over 85% of FP32 values have at least 1% relative error near KL 10^(-7) (FP16: 10^(-3)), and about 30% become negative at smaller divergences. More precision is not the cure: evaluated one precision higher, the same formulas still leave 7--51% of FP32 values significantly wrong for 22 of 23 configurations. Stable closed-form decompositions, compensated arithmetic, and analytic gradients remove over 97% of significant errors in the working format. Strict repairs eliminate significant errors on 7.2 million scored closed-form samples and correctly round all 567 million scored F.kl_div components. The errors affect parameter fitting, Bayesian decisions, identical-start distillation (up to 97% top-1 disagreement), KL-based layer rankings in a quantized LLM, and 19--59% of GPT-2 circuit edge scores. With the repaired code they all but vanish. Code and data: https://github.com/xi-xiaoran/stablekl

title: Analytic nuclear gradients for electronic resonances with the equation-of-motion coupled-cluster method and complex basis functions
summary: We present the general theory for and an efficient implementation of the analytic nuclear gradient for states which are metastable with respect to electronic decay within the equation-of-motion coupled-cluster singles-and-doubles family of methods using complex-scaled basis functions. We highlight the differences of our approach with the complex-absorbing potential method and outline a computational protocol for geometry optimisations and we use the method to compute equilibrium structures and harmonic vibrational frequencies of a number of temporary anion shape resonances and core-ionised Feshbach resonances.

title: Unpacking the Evaluators: How Configuration Shapes the Evaluation of Alignment in Explainable AI
summary: Explainable AI (XAI) evaluation fundamentally requires human-centered evaluation, assessing whether explanations align with human reasoning and expert knowledge. However, such evaluations often require expert-driven manual validation and are difficult to scale, leading to the widespread use of alignment-based metrics, where attribution maps are compared against predefined ground-truth (GT) representations. Despite their popularity, alignment evaluations are implicitly bias towards multiple design choices made during the evaluation process, for example GT representations, metric families, metric formulations (soft vs. hard), and thresholding strategies. In this paper, we formalize alignment evaluation as a structured evaluation configuration space through which the influence of these design choices can be systematically analyzed. We further introduce a structured alignment evaluation framework that models interactions between XAI methods, GT representations, metric families, metric formulations, and thresholding strategies across 2D and 3D synthetic and real-world datasets. In addition, we propose a novel taxonomy of XAI output behavior based on local entropy and boundary mass ratio, enabling structured characterization of attribution patterns for alignment evaluation. Our experiments reveal systematic flows (triples of XAI-GT-metric configurations), showing that alignment outcomes provide distinct behavior patterns under certain configurations, such as soft/hard metric implementations. We further observe varying levels of threshold sensitivity across metric families and attribution structures. These findings demonstrate that alignment evaluation cannot be treated as a fixed or invariant measure of explanation quality, and provide practical guidance for designing more reliable and behavior-aware XAI evaluation protocols.

title: HIVE-Bench: Evaluating Patch-Level Visual Representations for Egocentric Robot Manipulation
summary: Pretrained vision is a common start for robot learning, but most comparisons still score one pooled vector from a third-person image. Bimanual policies instead read dense patch tokens from cameras on the robot. We introduce HIVE-Bench: one shared flow-matching policy reads 20 encoders from seven families on 24 egocentric bimanual tasks, across adaptation, task sharing, and sweeps of data, model size, and layer. Keeping the patches matters. Averaging each view to one token removes most of the success, adaptation helps every pair we test, and one shared policy keeps most of the success of separate policies at a fraction of the updates. The same tokens are then scored with statistics, state and object readouts, published vision scores, and an inverse-dynamics readout. That readout of the commanded motion is one of the strongest measurements available before a policy is trained. Recognition, depth, and correspondence do not transfer reliably. Fine-tuning can improve the action readout even when other measurements move the other way, and no statistic is stable enough to replace a rollout before any deployment.

title: Noise-Immune Attractors in Stochastically Driven Non-Hermitian Systems
summary: Temporal stochastic fluctuations generically destroy quantum coherence and accelerate defect generation in driven quantum systems. Here, we demonstrate that non-Hermitian dynamics can fundamentally reverse this trend by stabilizing noise-resilient late-time states. By developing an exact noise master equation for non-Hermitian systems subject to Gaussian fluctuations, we uncover a projective noise-invariance mechanism governed by T-symmetry-broken Liouvillian attractors. This mechanism produces robust defect-density plateaus and yields an exact geometric classification into noise-independent, fully polarized, and continuously tunable regimes. We substantiate these results in an imbalanced-pairing non-Hermitian Kitaev model, a prototypical pseudo-Hermitian system, and propose their experimental observation in coupled photonic waveguides. Our findings identify non-Hermitian attractor dynamics as a versatile route to controlling noise-induced excitations beyond conventional anti-Kibble-Zurek scaling.

title: Nearly-Tight Oracle Complexity of Packing and Covering Linear Programs
summary: We settle the deterministic oracle complexity of packing and covering linear programs, as measured by the number of oracle queries to the constraint matrix modeled by left and right matrix-vector products, up to a logarithmic factor. We do so by providing nearly-matching upper and lower bounds. Our algorithm breaks the $1/ε^2$ barrier of width-independent, $(1+ε)$-multiplicative error parallel solvers from prior work, improving the scaling with the error $ε>0$ to $1/ε,$ with total number of arithmetic operations scaling near-linearly with $1/ε$ and the number of nonzero entries of the constraint matrix.

title: Free energy of the bipartite random assignment problem
summary: We compute the limiting free energy of the bipartite random assignment problem for every pseudodimension $d>0$ and every inverse temperature $λ> 0$ at the scale $n^{1/d}$. We show that the limit is given by a rigorous replica-symmetric formula determined by the unique solution of a recursive distributional equation on a Poisson-weighted infinite tree, confirming conjectures of Aldous and Talagrand. As a consequence, for a fixed inverse temperature $λ> 0$, we deduce exponential concentration of the cost of a Gibbs assignment and determine the exponential growth rate of the number of near-optimal assignments.

title: Fermionic dark linear seesaw with an anomalous Majoron
summary: We propose a minimal fermionic realisation of the $\textit{dark}$ linear seesaw with spontaneous breaking of lepton number. The small lepton-number-violating parameter responsible for linear-seesaw neutrino masses is generated radiatively by a $\textit{dark}$ sector consisting of a singlet and a doublet fermion, together with scalar singlets. The global U(1)$_L$ symmetry is broken to a residual $\mathcal{Z}_2$ under which the $\textit{dark}$ sector is odd. This breaking yields a Majoron $J$ and makes the lightest $\textit{dark}$ particle stable. The charged $\textit{dark}$ fermion acquires its mass solely from U(1)$_L$ breaking and thus induces an anomalous Majoron coupling to photons. Current bounds on this coupling exclude a massless Majoron for TeV-scale U(1)$_L$ breaking. We add a linear term that breaks lepton number softly and gives the Majoron a GeV-scale mass. Such a Majoron decays into two photons and can be probed at beam-dump experiments. We study the dark matter phenomenology, focusing on the case where the stable particle is a fermionic weakly interacting massive particle. We analyse how the framework can be tested through charged-lepton flavour-violating decays such as $μ\to eγ$, which receive contributions from both the $\textit{dark}$ and the seesaw sectors. Moreover, both sectors enhance the Majoron couplings to charged leptons, so that the Majoron-emitting decays $τ\to \ell J$ ($\ell = e,μ$) typically exceed $τ\to \ellγ$ by orders of magnitude and can probe parameter space beyond the reach of $μ\to eγ$.

title: BridgeMVS: Bridging Multi-View Stereo and Monodepth via Bidirectional Dynamic Fusion
summary: Multi-View Stereo (MVS) and Monocular Depth Estimation (MDE) provide complementary cues for dense 3D reconstruction. While MVS leverages explicit geometry for metric depth, it struggles in challenging regions where feature matching is unreliable. Conversely, MDE provides robust structural priors but typically yields scale-ambiguous results. Existing hybrid methods mainly exploit monocular cues in a unidirectional manner, leaving the mutual enhancement between MDE and MVS insufficiently explored. To address this limitation, we propose BridgeMVS, a unified cascaded multi-stage MVS framework that bridges monocular depth features and multi-view cost volume representations through Bidirectional Dynamic Fusion (BDF). At each stage, BDF performs dynamic mono-to-cost and cost-to-mono updates, where monocular structural features guide cost volume refinement for more robust MVS depth estimation, while multi-view geometric evidence recalibrates monocular representations to improve their metric-scale consistency. Furthermore, the fused monocular and multi-view representations are progressively propagated from coarse to fine stages and constrained by stage-wise relative-scale MDE supervision and metric-scale MVS supervision, enabling cross-branch interactions to benefit subsequent high-resolution depth estimation. In addition, BDF is designed as a plug-and-play module that can be conveniently integrated into existing cascaded MVS frameworks. Extensive experiments demonstrate that BridgeMVS achieves state-of-the-art performance on the DTU, Tanks-and-Temples, and ETH3D benchmarks, while simultaneously boosting the accuracy of monocular depth estimation. Notably, BridgeMVS ranks first on both the Tanks-and-Temples Intermediate and Advanced benchmarks. The source code is available at \href{https://github.com/JianfeiJ/BridgeMVS}{https://github.com/JianfeiJ/BridgeMVS}.

title: Beyond Domain Randomization: Real-World Policy Adaptation in Learned Dynamics for Legged Robots
summary: Reinforcement learning policies are often trained with static domain randomization for real-world deployment. However, real-world environments often exhibit unmodeled dynamic variations, such as payload changes or friction shifts, that lie outside the randomization distribution, leading to performance degradation upon deployment. We propose a framework that moves beyond static domain randomization by adapting a learned dynamics model to the deployed target conditions, with a concurrent teacher-student paradigm applied to both the policy and dynamics model. This framework integrates the dynamics model into an on-policy reinforcement learning pipeline, letting the performance of the policy align with the empirical target dynamics. Experimental validations on bipedal locomotion tasks demonstrate competitive adaptability under extreme physical variations, including a payload reaching 80% of self-weight and an oil-lubricated low-friction surface.

title: Light on GeV-scale seesaw
summary: The next generation of beam-dump and accelerator-neutrino experiments will probe GeV-scale sterile neutrinos with unprecedented sensitivity. However, the tiny active-sterile mixing predicted by the minimal seesaw mechanism is expected to remain out of reach. Oscillation data require at least two sterile neutrinos, $N_1$ and $N_2$, which may couple to the photon through a transition dipole. Such a coupling can radically change the picture, both by strongly enhancing sterile-neutrino production and by opening new decay channels. We identify charged-lepton pairs produced by an off-shell photon as the most promising experimental signature. We show that the seesaw band can be probed by the T2K near detector for sterile-neutrino masses $m_N\lesssim 500$ MeV, and by SHiP for $m_N\lesssim 5$ GeV. For a sufficiently large dipole, $d\gtrsim (10~\mathrm{TeV})^{-1}$, SHiP can selectively measure decay channels that require nonzero active-sterile mixing. This would give rise to a distinctive hierarchy of signatures, providing a direct test of the seesaw mechanism.

title: SignalCount: Approximate Counts with Structured and Semantic Predicates in Seconds
summary: Many applications store records with structured columns and a text document, and ask how many records in a filtered set meet a criterion that only a reader of the text can judge, such as "How many patients with type 2 diabetes, aged 40 to 70, stopped metformin because their blood sugar stayed high?" An interactive application needs this count in seconds, as the user types the criterion, to decide whether the matching set is worth materializing with a batch pipeline in which an LLM judges the records. Prior approximate query processing over such semantic predicates has an expensive model, the oracle, label a sample at query time, so every query waits for the oracle. We present SignalCount, a production system that answers COUNT queries with structured and semantic predicates and calls no oracle at query time, even for ad-hoc criteria. Its oracle is the production LLM judge, and the judge's logged verdicts calibrate, offline, the fast classifier that already runs in front of the judge. At query time, SignalCount counts the filtered set exactly and draws a uniform sample of at most 1,000 records in one columnar scan, scores the sample with the classifier, and multiplies the average calibrated probability by the exact count. Its 90% interval combines a sampling term with one-sided, rate-dependent margins for calibration error, fitted by split conformal prediction across tenants. In a multi-tenant production deployment, latency has a p99 of 3.8 s and stays flat as the filtered set grows beyond the sample. On tenants held out from fitting, the interval covers the count that the production pipeline returns in 92% of estimates, although estimates run about 15% high in aggregate, because a calibration nearly unbiased per record is still biased per criterion.

title: What Quality Engineers Need to Know About Generative AI: Structured Data Extraction
summary: In this expository paper, we explain how quality engineers can use large language models (LLMs) and vision-language models (VLMs) for structured data extraction. We introduce the relevant concepts, discuss structured extraction from a measurement-system perspective, and demonstrate its implementation in R and Python. We then present two freely available web-based applications (apps): (a) extracting information from automotive recall notices and (b) monitoring quality engineering research on arXiv. To ensure the accuracy of our AI-driven structured extraction, human evaluators validated the results. In the first app, four reviewers assessed information extracted from 30 recall notices using two models, with 98.6% of the 720 field-level ratings judged fully correct. In the second app, 21 authors evaluated information extracted from 45 of their arXiv papers. All paper summaries were rated mostly correct or correct, although the evaluations identified problems with some classification fields and mathematical expressions. These results demonstrate the practical potential of structured data extraction while emphasizing the need to validate the extracted information. We make both apps and their source code publicly available so that readers can adapt the approach to their own applications.

title: Torcalia.jl: An MPI-based Runtime System for Asynchronous Task Parallelism in Julia
summary:
Designed to address the two-language problem, the Julia programming language provides a powerful platform for developing high-performance scientific computing and machine learning applications. Such applications increasingly exhibit irregular, adaptive, or data-driven workloads for which traditional bulk-synchronous parallel (BSP) models often struggle to efficiently exploit the available parallelism. Asynchronous many-task (AMT) runtime systems offer a compelling alternative, decomposing computations into fine-grained tasks that are dynamically scheduled across the hierarchical architecture of modern HPC systems.
  This paper introduces Torcalia$.$jl, a Julia package designed to orchestrate the asynchronous execution of tasks across both shared and distributed memory environments. Built on top of MPI$.$jl and Julia's native multithreading, Torcalia employs a dependency-aware task scheduling scheme that combines the work-sharing and work-stealing paradigms to achieve adaptive load balancing. Tasks can be nested arbitrarily, enabling applications to exploit multiple levels of parallelism, while application-level distributed shared memory (DSM) extends task-based shared-memory programming to multi-node clusters. Beyond task-based programming, the proposed library supports skeletal programming, providing high-level abstractions that facilitate the implementation of parallel applications at scale. Evaluated on the ARIS supercomputer using four diverse workloads, Torcalia demonstrates strong scalability, reducing wall-clock time by up to 18.1% compared with Dagger, a state-of-the-art task-based engine in Julia. The source code of Torcalia$.$jl is publicly available at https://github.com/CEID-HPCLAB/Torcalia.jl.

title: Trallie: from Free-Form Text to Structured Data with LLMs
summary: Trallie is an open-source framework that leverages large language models (LLMs) to perform information extraction (IE) from natural language sources with or without user guidance. Unlike conventional approaches that rely on extensive labeled datasets or domain-specific training, Trallie enables the conversion of unstructured data into structured formats with minimal or no representative examples. The framework is designed with three key objectives: (i) reducing manual annotation by harnessing prompt-based zero-shot and few-shot capabilities of modern LLMs, (ii) flexibly parsing diverse document formats (i.e., HTML, PDF, TXT, and JSON), and (iii) improving accessibility for non-expert users by automatically inducing schemas from document collections, which can then be refined for extraction. We evaluate Trallie with open-weight LLMs on FDA 510(k) documents and on movie and university websites from SWDE. It outperforms previously reported systems when the target attributes are provided for text extraction and is competitive when it must discover attributes for the schema automatically. The project is available at https://github.com/PiSchool/trallie

title: Bridging the Semantic Gap from Natural Language Specifications to RTL with Layered Formal Guidance
summary: While large language models (LLMs) have shown promise in generating register-transfer level (RTL) code from natural-language specifications, their reliability remains limited on designs with complex control logic and temporal behavior. This stems from a fundamental semantic gap: high-level natural language often leaves implementation-critical details underspecified, forcing LLMs to infer unstated assumptions. This paper presents Layered Formal Guidance, a novel framework that bridges this semantic gap by using formal properties as an intermediate semantic layer between natural-language specifications and RTL generation. Our framework applies formal guidance across three layers: property-driven specification augmentation before generation, property-consistency checking after generation, and counterexample-guided refinement after checking. Experiments on RTLLM benchmarks and various open-source IP designs demonstrate that our framework achieves higher functional correctness and lower sampled output-trace diversity. Furthermore, we show that Layered Formal Guidance can flexibly augment both general-purpose LLMs and domain-specific models to substantially improve their generation reliability.

title: Object Count Generalization Is an Interface Problem: Warping a Frozen Skill Instead of Retraining It
summary: Reinforcement learning policies for robot manipulation degrade when the number of objects N in the scene grows beyond the training range. This is a covariate shift that also changes the dimension of the state. We propose WAVE (Warping Actions and Views of an Expert), which extends a pretrained single-object skill to many objects without updating its weights. WAVE has three parts. First, a selection policy picks the one object the robot works on next. Second, a warping policy reads a local view of the scene around that object, whose size does not depend on N. It emits a multiplier and an offset for every quantity the skill reads and every action it outputs. Third, the skill acts under this affine warp. It is shown a scene that holds a single object, while the warp steers it around the objects it is not shown and edits the actions that are sent to the robot. Both the selection and warping policies are trained with PPO on the multi-object reward and use the skill as a black box, so WAVE is task-general and skill-agnostic. It requires only that the skill was trained on the same embodiment and that every object has a goal pose. We also bound the number of attempts needed to place all N objects, assuming positive expected net progress per attempt, and measure this progress for each object count. We evaluate WAVE on cube arrangement tasks with a gantry robot and with a Franka Panda arm. Trained with at most nine cubes, it generalizes zero-shot to several times its training count, on the gantry to scenes of up to thirty cubes. Published methods that learn multi-object manipulation show count generalization up to six objects. Fine-tuning the skill, learning from the same local view without it, and an entity transformer, even when distilled from the pretrained skill, all collapse within their training counts under the same training budget.

title: Fate of Vainshtein Screening for UV/IR Mixing with a $P(X)$ Higgs Classicalizer
summary: Classicalization is a non-Wilsonian framework in which an effective field theory self-completes above its strong-coupling scale by generating semiclassical objects that decay into many soft quanta, thereby realizing ultraviolet-infrared mixing. A key requirement of this mechanism is that the force carrier be lighter than the strong-coupling scale. A natural application would be to embed classicalization in the electroweak Higgs sector to address the little hierarchy problem. In this work, we investigate whether Higgs classicalization can occur within the $P(X)$ class of gauged k-essence and k-chameleon models. For classicalization to occur, the theory must support Vainshtein screening around a sharply localized source. Our results show that it fails to do so, even when one attempts to engineer a symbiosis with chameleon screening through a gauge kinetic function, owing to a strong-coupling breakdown inside the screening region. These $P(X)$ theories therefore fail to provide a suitable framework for Higgs classicalization. Nevertheless, we emphasize that our results, obtained for a specific class of models, should not be interpreted as a no-go theorem for Higgs classicalization.

title: Intent-Conditioned Argument Mediation for Tool-Using LLM Agents: Blocking Trusted-but-Unauthorized Arguments
summary: LLM agents turn a user's request and retrieved content into tool calls, and a call can reach the wrong recipient, endpoint, file or participant. Argument-level provenance blocks such values when they come from untrusted content, but accepts a trusted value that the user never requested. IntentFlow, a mediation layer between an unmodified planner and its tools, checks each authority-bearing argument against an intent contract and a provenance policy. On a synthetic benchmark of 200 attacks (oracle intent and injection labels, declared roles), attack success falls from 50.5% with provenance alone to 12.0% [8.2-17.2%]; every remaining success alters a content or payload field. IntentFlow wrongly blocks none of 200 paired benign tasks and 4 of 50 hard ones. On 50 trusted-but-unauthorized attacks, provenance-only mediation executes all 50 and IntentFlow none; a CaMeL-style check also blocks all 50 but rejects 16 of 50 benign tasks. On an offline AgentDojo-derived replay, IntentFlow blocks all 20 attacks at 75% benign success, as does a CaMeL-style check; a Progent-style allowlist blocks 19 and keeps all benign tasks. With one live planner and the same oracles, the mediator blocked all 17 corrupted calls proposed in 110 attacks.

title: Transport-Safe Evaluation of LLM Agents: Trajectory-Dependent Judge Error and Anytime-Valid Auditing
summary: Large language model (LLM) agents are often ranked by an LLM judge whose error rates are measured once and reused for every agent. The corrected success rates can then be biased when the judge's errors depend on the trajectory and agents differ in the trajectories they produce for successes or failures. We derive the exact asymptotic bias and give a chain of checks from identification to simultaneous ranks. On a four-agent semi-synthetic benchmark, a scalar correction with oracle calibration has maximum bias 0.245 and mean pointwise coverage 0.016, and never recovers the full ranking (0/250 replications). Augmented inverse-probability weighting (AIPW) with a uniform or a design-aware random audit keeps the maximum bias below 0.003, with mean pointwise coverage of 0.939 and 0.950. In a 48-cell stress test, effective target support rises only from 0.209 to 0.805 as calibration grows from 600 to 4,800 labels, while audited AIPW keeps a mean absolute error of 0.018-0.020. Without calibration support, or with judge dependence within an externally justified bound, we report valid bounds or sensitivity sets and carry them into rank sets. An e-process confidence sequence stays valid, for a stable target, under predictable adaptive auditing and arbitrary stopping.

title: EgoDepth-Bench: Benchmarking Metric Depth for Egocentric Manipulation
summary: We introduce EgoDepth-Bench, comprising 941,233 synchronized samples collected across 37 distinct physical environments. Each sample combines six calibrated RGB views with metric depth in the native fisheye view, reconstructed from five active-infrared stereo modules. A calibrated ball-bar confirms millimeter-level geometric accuracy, with a median error of 1.27 mm on a known sphere spacing. Environment-held-out splits enable evaluation of generalization to unseen environments. Across monocular, stereo, and multi-view models, the benchmark measures both depth accuracy and prediction coverage, including on hands and objects. Fine-tuning MapAnything on EgoDepth-Bench reduces metric AbsRel from 0.708 to 0.091 and scale-aligned AbsRel from 0.327 to 0.072 on unseen environments. These results demonstrate that EgoDepth-Bench provides effective supervision and enables rigorous evaluation of metric and relative depth estimation in egocentric manipulation. The project page provides the evaluation code and interactive RGB-depth sequences.

title: Learning and Dynamic Route Recommendation Under Unknown Traveler Compliance and Road Conditions
summary: Route planning during evacuations and other large-scale egress operations is inherently dynamic: the planner's recommendations affect future congestion on the roads, influence whether travelers accept their guidance, and determine what the planner can learn from the travelers' actual route choices. In this paper, we consider stochastic dynamic route recommendation to many travelers over a finite horizon under uncertain compliance and road conditions. In each period, a planner assigns routes that lead different origins' traveler groups to safe destinations, and travelers either follow the recommendation or revert to a preferred route. We model compliance using a logistic model and learn its unknown coefficients from observed route travel. We also filter the state of road conditions from noisy telemetry, and use a performance state to capture how the quality of past route recommendation affects travelers' future compliance. To determine the route assignment policy, we formulate a finite-horizon, belief-state dynamic program, show that the information state is sufficient for optimal Markov control, and develop an approximation that combines compliance beliefs with proximal policy optimization (PPO) using a Dirichlet actor over feasible route shares. We conduct numerical studies on instances of Eastern Massachusetts highway network data under different uncertain road conditions and compliance behavior. We demonstrate the efficiency and effectiveness of the PPO method and the value of dynamic adaptive solutions, against static routes. Our solutions reduce the mean and upper-tail costs of all travelers relative to myopic policy benchmarks, even when these benchmarks know the true compliance coefficients. Moreover, updating beliefs and the performance state dynamically also reduces the total cost under accurate, biased, and diffuse priors.

title: Modeling of Chemically Reactive Gas Flows for Multi-Scale Problems
summary: Accurate modeling of chemical reactions plays a key role in the investigation of high-temperature flows. The Direct Simulation Monte Carlo (DSMC) method provides highly accurate solutions for such flows. However, its computational cost becomes prohibitive for low Knudsen regimes. Particle-based continuum methods employing the Bhatnagar-Gross-Krook (BGK) or Fokker-Planck approximations have gained increasing attention in recent years, improve computational efficiency in low-Knudsen regimes by modeling relaxation processes rather than binary collisions, while retaining the particle approach that enables straightforward coupling with DSMC. In the last years, different continuum-based models in the open-source particle code PICLas have been extended to simulate gas mixtures with internal energy modes. The present work focuses on modeling of chemically reactive gas mixtures in the Ellipsoidal Statistical BGK model. Model accuracy is assessed for two test cases of a reactive gases confined in a reservoir.

title: Hard to Translate, Harder to Detect: Human Analysis Remains Essential in AI Meme Translation
summary: We present a dataset and evaluation setup for a problem in creative machine translation: translating culturally loaded passages that carry much of a text's meaning and humor that may depend on subtle or implicit discourse. We study Soviet comedy quotations that function as memes in Russian-language communication. Off-the-shelf difficulty estimators do not find these passages; current models searching the web find most but not all of them, but their own analyses of the difficulty do not help translation as well as a human-validated one. Given a brief human-validated analysis of why each passage is difficult, older models improve modestly; the strongest current translators (GPT-6 Sol and Claude Opus 5.5) improve more, and in human evaluation GPT-6 Sol comes close to the approved references on most films. Newer models have thus become much better at using such an analysis while still not reliably producing it themselves. We release (1) a dataset of five films' Russian subtitles with their audience-selected culturally salient passages, human-validated analyses, and reference translations (into English, Galician, and Spanish), together with every full-film LLM translation and evaluation produced in this study; and (2) an item-level MQM-style evaluation protocol that measures translator and evaluator noise to set the number of runs the evaluation needs, and whose automatic version tracks human judgment of these passages, which reference-free neural metrics do not, whether they score the whole text or the passages alone.

title: Lowering the Bar for Everyone: Hidden Validation-Seeking Goals in Empathetic RL
summary:
When RL learns from the reactions of many users, the policy usually cannot see what each user wants. We ask what it learns from users who privately want validation: to validate them alone (targeting), or to lower its bar for endorsing everyone (a threshold shift). We answer this in one setting, empathetic RL against LLM-simulated users (RLVER, GRPO, Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct): we vary only the share of validation-seeking users (0--50%; RLVER's default: 24.6%) and evaluate on 1,000 Reddit AITA posts with community fault verdicts.
  The policy shifts its threshold. Endorsement of at-fault posters rises by 3--4 percentage points per 10 points of share; without such users the Qwen model stays at base, and the effect persists at matched KL and under a goal-blind reward. Signal-detection analysis shows that the criterion for endorsing falls while discrimination between at-fault and not-at-fault posters does not decline. An explicit request to be told if one is wrong gives no measurable protection: at-fault posters who make it receive nearly the same rise as those who do not (+0.11 vs. +0.13). When the goal is stated during training, the policy instead largely targets, endorsing seekers regardless of fault.
  Standard sycophancy and empathy benchmarks miss the shift; five of six usable released empathetic-RL checkpoints also endorse at-fault posters who ask for honesty more than their base models, though a pre-registered prediction for two held for only one. The user mix is a training hyperparameter to audit and report.

title: Archival X-Ray Observations of the Eclipsing Algol-type Binary TV~Cassiopeiae
summary: TV~Cassiopeiae (TV~Cas) is an eclipsing Algol-type binary with a B9\,V primary and an evolved late-type secondary in a 1.81-day orbit. We examine six serendipitous Chandra and two XMM-Newton observations spanning 2003--2012. The supplied Chandra spectra show thermal plasma near 1~keV and sub-solar fitted abundances, with an additional hotter component in one observation. EPIC-pn fits improve substantially with two temperatures: approximately 0.74/1.39~keV in 2003 and 0.87/2.16~keV in 2012. At 240~pc their nominal intrinsic 0.3--8~keV luminosities are $7.1\times10^{30}$ and $1.2\times10^{31}$~erg~s$^{-1}$, but residual structure, particularly in 2012, and response-calibration uncertainties limit physical interpretation. A prominent flare-like event occurs in Chandra ObsID 08458 (2006-11-04). The longest observation carried out in 2012 pn light curve spans approximately 82\% of an orbit and shows no conspicuous deep eclipse at the predicted secondary conjunction. An exploratory multi-epoch fold contains apparent troughs, but heterogeneous responses, intrinsic variability, and ephemeris uncertainty prevent a unique orbital interpretation. Thermal spectra and flare-like behavior favor a magnetically active secondary corona. The available products do not securely determine a coronal scale height, an orbital modulation amplitude, elemental abundance changes, or the fractional contributions of other unresolved emitters.

title: Hierarchical Multi-Timescale Deep Reinforcement Learning for QoS-Aware AI-RAN Configuration
summary: Configuring radio access networks (RANs) for heterogeneous services requires coordinating radio parameters whose effects on throughput, delay, and reliability are closely coupled and evolve over different timescales. This paper presents a hierarchical deep reinforcement learning (DRL) framework for joint, QoS-aware RAN configuration that aligns the learning structure with the real-time, near-real-time, and non-real-time control loops of O-RAN that are also adopted by AI-RAN. Three proximal policy optimization agents jointly select per-user modulation and coding schemes, user-to-bandwidth-part (BWP) assignments, per-BWP transmit power, numerology, and BWP bandwidth weights, at three timescales. The agents share a QoS-aware objective combining throughput demand satisfaction with delay and reliability penalties. We extend ns-3 5G-LENA and integrate it with Ray RLlib through ns3-ai to support the required radio controls, network observations, and hierarchical policy execution. We evaluate the agents' performance in a nine-cell downlink network with inter-cell interference, varying user populations, and mixed URLLC, gaming, conversational-video, and video-streaming traffic. Compared with the baseline 5G-NR RAN, our trained hierarchical DRL agents substantially reduce URLLC and conversational-video delays, lower the residual block error rate, and prevent the near-starvation of the weakest flows, trading off slightly lower throughput for high-rate video streaming under capacity-limited conditions.

title: How Many Parameters Does Forecasting Need? A Survey and Code-Level Audit of Lightweight Long-Term Time Series Forecasting
summary: Long-term time series forecasting supports decisions in energy, transportation, weather and finance, where forecasts are produced continuously and often on constrained hardware. Recent work has moved in two directions. One scales Transformers and pre-trained foundation models to millions or hundreds of millions of parameters. The other shows that models with only hundreds to tens of thousands of parameters remain competitive on the standard benchmarks. Existing surveys organize forecasting models by backbone and treat efficiency as a side topic, so the reasons these small models work, and the way their sizes are reported, remain unexamined. This survey focuses on lightweight long-term forecasting. It provides a taxonomy of about thirty-five models in six families, with a common notation and an architecture diagram for each core model. It offers a structured-linear view in which the smallest models are linear maps restricted by frequency truncation or period folding, and it tests each restriction in closed form on eight benchmarks. It complements the literature review with an audit of sixteen official code repositories, which reproduces published parameter counts and reveals reporting gaps of up to 289 times. Finally, it gives practical guidance on model selection and reporting, and summarizes open problems.

title: FlexVSR: Continuous-Scale Super-Resolution for Streaming Video Generation
summary: Real-time streaming video generation has gained rapid momentum in live content creation and interactive media. Deploying such systems in practice requires flexible scaling factors to accommodate diverse source resolutions, target displays, and computational budgets. However, extending fixed-scale generative video super-resolution (VSR) to varying target scales poses two challenges: downsampling from a larger fixed scale incurs redundant cost, while re-optimizing the diffusion transformer (DiT) is costly and alters the shared generative prior. To address both, we propose FlexVSR, a decoupled framework for continuous-scale streaming generative VSR with supervision at only a few scales. Our key insight is that naively resampling fixed-scale latents onto a new target grid induces scale-dependent input mismatch, which can be effectively addressed through parameter-efficient, scale-aware adaptation of the latent interface without updating the DiT. To this end, FlexVSR introduces ReLSA (Refined Latent Scale Adaptation), a lightweight latent adapter that constructs and refines target-grid latents before they enter the DiT, enabling a shared frozen VSR prior to generalize across continuous scales with only 0.274M trainable parameters and an adaptation cost of 7.3 H100 GPU-hours, while introducing no additional temporal dependencies and preserving the native causal streaming protocol. Extensive experiments demonstrate competitive or superior reconstruction and temporal quality, lower latency than most native-scale streaming baselines and offline methods, and effective generalization to unseen continuous scales, filling the continuous-scale gap in real-time streaming generative VSR.

title: Strain-induced non-trivial band topology and large magnetoresistance in epitaxial SrTaO$_3$ thin films
summary: Epitaxial thin films of complex transition metal oxides constitute an ideal platform for realizing correlated topological phases through strain engineering of crystal symmetry and band topology. Here, we investigate the electronic transport properties and the band structure of the 5$d^1$ paramagnetic metal SrTaO$_3$ thin film under epitaxial compressive strain. The film exhibits a large non-saturating quasi-quadratic magnetoresistance (MR) and a nonlinear Hall effect characteristic of two-band transport, together with the field induced re-entrant metallic behavior. The violation of Kohler's scaling further corroborates the scattering from multiple bands. Semiclassical two-band analysis yields carrier densities and mobilities of the order $\sim 10^{21}~\mathrm{cm^{-3}}$ and $\sim 10^{4}~\mathrm{cm^2 V^{-1} s^{-1}}$, respectively. The observed large mobility and unsaturated MR, indicates the presence of a non-trivial band structure. Consistent with this, results from density functional theory calculations and tight binding model studies reveal that the stable structure has an octahedral rotation $a^0a^0c^+$, where the non-symmorphic symmetry ensures the presence of topological nodal lines yielding finite Berry curvature in the vicinity of the Fermi level. Besides the nodal line, trivial electron and hole pockets exist near the Fermi level, contributing to electron transport. These findings establish that epitaxial strain drives SrTaO$_3$ into a nontrivial topological semimetal, a phase inaccessible in the bulk counterpart.

title: THeatA: Transport- and Heating-aware QEC simulation with Cooling Strategies for QCCD Trapped-Ion Systems
summary: The quantum charge-coupled device (QCCD) architecture is a promising approach to scalable trapped-ion quantum computing, enabling flexible qubit interactions by transporting ions between dedicated trap zones. Programs for such systems require operations beyond conventional circuit primitives: ion shuttling, physical SWAPs, trap splitting and merging, and cooling. Motional excitation accumulated during transport increases the mean phonon number of ions and degrades the fidelity of the two-qubit Molmer-Sorensen gates. However, existing quantum error correction (QEC) simulation frameworks do not jointly track per-ion motional excitation and explicitly schedule cooling operations with their transport time and heating costs. We develop a full-stack software framework for QEC experiments and simulations on linear QCCD systems with a single ion species, comprising an intermediate representation (IR) supporting QCCD-native operations, a compiler that translates syndrome-extraction circuits into the IR, and a heating-aware noise-injection pipeline that generates noisy Stim circuits. The compiler updates the mean phonon number of each ion throughout the schedule, and the pipeline derives gate-dependent error rates from the tracked phonon states and per-ion timing, enabling the evaluation of finite-size logical-error scaling of the rotated surface code under transport- and heating-aware noise. We show that transport-induced heating prevents logical error rates from decreasing with increasing code distance under the evaluated conditions, and that indirectly cooling the ion pairs involved in two-qubit gates, by merging them with precooled coolant ions immediately before each gate, restores this decrease. By sweeping the duration and post-cooling mean phonon number of an abstract cooling instruction, we characterize their trade-off and identify the region in which logical-error scaling is maintained.

title: Empirical Margin Sensitivity: An Interventional Neuron-Level Probe of Post-Trained Medical LLMs
summary: Medical post-training raises benchmark accuracy, but accuracy does not show which internal components a model's decisions depend on, or whether components that support one benchmark also support another. We apply the weight-space intervention paradigm of ROME and MEMIT at the granularity of one MLP down-projection column. Our measurement, Empirical Margin Sensitivity (EMS), replaces each coordinate magnitude of a column by its mean while preserving the column's sign pattern and L1 scale, and records the resulting change in the logit margin between the correct option and its hardest-wrong competitor. This isolates the margin's dependence on a column's fine-grained coordinate structure while the column stays in place. We discover high-EMS columns (anchors) on MedQA in ten public checkpoints (four general-purpose bases and six medical post-trained variants) across the Gemma, Llama, Qwen, and AFM families, and measure the same columns on MedMCQA and PubMedQA. Mean-ablating each discovered anchor set lowers MedQA accuracy in all six post-trained models, by 6 to 28 points. In the two pure-SFT checkpoints, crushing anchors raises the PubMedQA margin on correctly answered items (negative EMS), and anchors with this property sit significantly deeper than the same model's other anchors; the four checkpoints trained with RL or mixed recipes show positive PubMedQA EMS and no significant depth shift.
