The ML-identified stars occupy distinct regions in colour-magnitude and Gaia-2MASS diagrams, and comparison with stellar isochrones combined with Gaia distances allows estimates of their masses and ages. Spatial distributions show that O-rich AGB stars dominate the inner Galaxy, while C-rich AGB stars are concentrated toward the anti-Galactic centre. Vertical profiles indicate that massive O-rich (5-8 M$_\odot$) stars remain near the Galactic mid-plane, whereas C-rich (2.3-2.5 M$_\odot$) and low-mass O-rich (1-1.5 M$_\odot$) AGB stars are more vertically extended, with scale heights that increase with decreasing stellar mass and increasing stellar ages. C-rich AGB stars trace the Galactic warp at intermediate ages (1 Gyr), with warp amplitudes appearing larger than those traced by Cepheids. Intermediate-mass O-rich AGB stars (~300 Myr) show tentative correspondence with several spiral arm features, while the C-rich distribution is too smooth for reliable identification with the current sample. These results highlight AGB stars as powerful probes of stellar evolution and Galactic dynamical processes.

title: Onset of quantum chaos in a family of two-dimensional conformal field theories
summary: We exhibit random matrix statistics in the scaling dimensions of non-BPS primary operators in a family of two-dimensional conformal field theories. Specifically, we consider the sigma model with K3 target space and $\mathcal N=(4,4)$ supersymmetry in a neighborhood of the Kummer orbifold point $\mathbb T^4/\mathbb Z_2$. At the free-fermion radius, the spin-zero spectrum of the $\mathbb Z_2^4$-invariant sector is exactly degenerate at integer energies. The exactly marginal blow-up deformations that preserve this symmetry form a four-dimensional space, whose directions we parametrize by unit quaternions. Along each deformation direction, we compute the first-order splitting of the degenerate levels, i.e., the leading anomalous dimensions as the coupling goes to zero. In sectors where all exact symmetries are resolved, including a hidden $\mathbb Z_2$ at the even levels, the non-zero first-order shifts along a generic direction follow the Gaussian orthogonal ensemble (GOE), as we verify by computing several spectral diagnostics. We compare quantitatively with the well-known singlet deformation, which has enhanced symmetry: even after all its known symmetries are resolved, its first-order spectrum has exact degeneracies, its gap ratio approaches the GOE value only slowly as the energy increases, and its unfolded spectrum lacks the long-range rigidity of the GOE.

title: The MURALES survey. IX. MUSE observations and results for 3C radio sources at 0.3 < z < 0.82
summary: This is the ninth paper in the MUse RAdio Loud Emission lines Snapshot (MURALES) project series, presenting the results of observations of 3C radio sources obtained with the VLT/MUSE integral field spectrograph. Here, we investigate the morphology and kinematics of the extended emission line regions (EELRs) of 26 radio galaxies at intermediate redshift 0.3 < z < 0.82 and their relation with the radio ejecta. EELRs are observed in all but 4 of the 26 sources extending as far as 160 kpc from the host galaxy. They show different morphologies and kinematics usually related with the radio properties. The five sources associated with the smaller radio sources show highly disturbed gas kinematics. Several EELRs have a filamentary morphology, often forming bubbles inflated by the radio lobes. The more extended EELRs usually have elongated morphologies and show well-ordered rotation. We then confirm the general results obtained from the study of the source at lower redshift: radio galaxies are surrounded by super-disks, that is, structures of ionized gas on scales of many tens of kiloparsec, whose properties depend on a combination of the evolutionary state of the radio source and its orientation with respect to the super-disks.

title: Charge Exchange Illuminates Turbulent Cold-Hot Interfaces
summary: Cold-hot interfaces are ubiquitous in the multiphase circumgalactic medium (CGM), galactic winds, and the Galactic Center (GC), yet their microscopic contact regions are difficult to observe. Charge exchange (CX), in which a highly ionized metal ion captures an electron from a neutral donor and emits soft X-ray lines, directly probes these interfaces. We develop a subgrid CX model coupled to a nonequilibrium ionization (NEI) network in hydrodynamic simulations of radiative turbulent mixing layers. CX soft X-rays are confined to a thin, highly corrugated cold-hot interface (corrugation factor $\sim10$), whereas thermal emission fills the hot phase. Turbulent transport sustains high-charge ions at $T\sim 10^4$-$10^5$ K, where they encounter neutral donors. The low-temperature O VIII fraction exceeds that in a uniformly cooling isobaric parcel, demonstrating the importance of mixing to the ionization history. CX depletes this cool ion population, while continued entrainment maintains the supply. Including a metagalactic ionizing background changes the ion distribution and enhances CX surface brightness by a factor of a few in our CGM comparison, but preserves the cool origin of most CX emission. In the limit of sufficient neutral column, CX surface brightness is ion-supply limited: higher donor density increases local emissivity but shortens the reaction layer. The system-wide CX-to-thermal soft X-ray ratio also depends on the volume-to-interface scale $V/A_{\rm int}$, making CX a potential probe of multiphase structure in the CGM, galactic winds, and the GC.

title: Posterior Matching Distillation
summary: Diffusion distillation accelerates image and video generation by compressing a pretrained teacher's iterative sampling process into a few network evaluations. Distribution-based methods achieve this by matching the student's output distribution to the teacher's. This matching is often driven by reverse-KL objectives, whose mode-seeking bias favors dominant teacher modes at the expense of diversity across samples. We introduce Posterior Matching Distillation (PMD), a new member of the distribution-based distillation family that combines mode-covering posterior sampling with any-step generation. At zero population loss, PMD recovers the teacher's full posterior of clean images at each trained noise level. Its stochastic student supports any-step sampling budgets within the trained timestep grid without further training. To learn these posteriors, PMD matches exponentially reweighted averages of student samples conditioned on a fixed noisy state to corresponding teacher posterior means. Under Gaussian corruption, exponentially tilted posterior mean is a single teacher evaluation at a shifted input. We prove that, matching tilted means over an open neighborhood uniquely identifies the full posterior. PMD thus supervises the entire conditional distribution through a family of mean constraints, without any auxiliary student-score network. Experiments on SDXL and FLUX.2 [klein] 4B demonstrate that PMD achieves the best FID among 4-step methods on both models, while maintaining competitive or leading performance across prompt-alignment and perceptual-quality metrics.

title: RL Post-Training in Diffusion Transformers Is Activation Steering
summary: Reinforcement learning (RL) post-training substantially improves the visual quality, text rendering, and compositional accuracy of diffusion transformers. Because capabilities such as rendering requested text or composing multiple objects are inherently prompt-dependent, a natural hypothesis is that improving them requires learning complex, input-dependent transformations. To isolate how much of these gains an input-independent shift explains, we probe each RL-tuned model with a deliberately simple parameterization: a fixed set of steering vectors added to the block outputs of the frozen base model. On SD3.5-M, these vectors hold 65x fewer parameters than the RL-tuned LoRA (0.29M against 18.8M). We fit them to match the velocity predictions of public RL-tuned checkpoints, with no reward in the objective. Although the vectors are identical for every prompt, token, and sampling seed, they recover 90.0-96.3% of the reward gains of six RL-tuned image models, and 89.8% and 111.9% on two RL-tuned video models. Initialized at zero and trained with online RL, the vectors alone exceed the reward gains of weight-based RL on text rendering (OCR) and human preference (PickScore) on SD3.5-M. A constant shift thus suffices for most of the gain of policy-gradient RL post-training: without new input-dependent transformations, it steers the pretrained generator toward what it can already compute.

title: AnyVIO: Feed-Forward Streaming Visual-Inertial Odometry Across Platforms
summary: Geometric foundation models (GFMs) estimate camera mo- tion and scene structure from images without requiring ex- pert parameter tuning, but either lack metric scale or rely on learned priors to infer scale, which is unobservable from monocular images alone. Inertial sensing offers a way to observe metric scale, but existing methods add inertial in- formation through a filter or factor graph, which reintro- duces bespoke parameter tuning and optimization costs that can grow with the trajectory. To bridge this gap, we present AnyVIO, a real-time, feed-forward streaming model for monocular visual-inertial odometry (VIO), which combines a streaming GFM with an inertial foundation model (IFM). Both the GFM and IFM predict the metric motion between consecutive frames, and a lightweight learned fusion head quantifies the reliability of each estimate and blends them in a single forward pass. Across nine datasets recorded from cars, legged and ground robots, and handheld and head- mounted devices, AnyVIO reduces the metric position error of its visual model by 36% while publishing each pose esti- mate 70 ms after an image is received. We further deploy AnyVIO onboard two real vehicles at up to 140 km/h, where it remains accurate in poor lighting and heavy dust.

title: TideCache: Efficient Hybrid LLM Serving with Transparent Cache Management and Layer-Wise Streaming
summary: Hybrid architectures have become mainstream among open-weight language models. Their global-attention and bounded-state layers maintain heterogeneous caches whose demands vary with context length and concurrency. We present TideCache, a serving system on CPU--GPU superchips with three components for allocating GPU memory among caches and managing their residency across GPU and host memory. The Transparent Cache Pool redistributes physical pages among cache components behind fixed virtual addresses, preserving cache layouts and backend interfaces. The Cache Streamer uses computation intervals provided by bounded-state layers to prefetch the next global-attention layer's prefix into GPU slots shared across global-attention layers, reducing GPU residency while overlapping layer-wise transfers with computation. Generated KV remains resident. The Request Scheduler selects resident or streamed execution and triggers capacity adjustments according to request size and queue state. Together, they let HBM released by streaming accommodate other cache components and additional requests. Implemented in SGLang and evaluated on GB300 and GH200 across seven model/platform configurations, TideCache completes up to 2.04x as many agent turns, reduces overall P50 per-token latency by 20--59%, and improves agent P50 TTFT by 1.40--3.05x compared with SGLang with HiCache.

title: Every galaxy is a radio source: a stellar-mass dependent minimum 150 MHz luminosity identified in the LoTSS Deep Fields
summary: The second data release of the LOFAR Two-metre Sky Survey (LoTSS) Deep Fields includes the deepest wide-field 150 MHz mosaics in existence, covering the ELAIS-N1 field. Combining these radio observations with star-formation rate (SFR) and stellar mass estimates for 113,228 near-infrared selected galaxies derived using Prospector, we re-examine the relationship between galaxies' 150 MHz luminosities ($L_{150\rm{MHz}}$), SFRs and stellar masses. We not only recover the established radio luminosity-SFR relation and its dependence on stellar mass, but also discover a mass-dependent minimum radio luminosity that is independent of SFR. This behaviour is especially evident in galaxies with low specific SFR (sSFR $\equiv$ SFR/$M_*$), at $L_{150\rm MHz} \sim 10^{20}-10^{22}$ W Hz$^{-1}$, where star-forming galaxies are expected to dominate. The non-stellar emission is consistent with low-level accretion onto supermassive black holes (i.e. weak active galactic nuclei, AGN), spanning effective Eddington-scaled accretion rates $λ_{\rm Edd} \sim 10^{-5}-10^{-4}$, suggesting that radio emission due to accretion is widespread and effectively continuous. A two-component model combining star formation- and accretion-driven emission reproduces the observed trends, demonstrating that AGN activity can bias radio-based SFR estimates. The low radio luminosities probed in this work provide a first glimpse of the populations that will be routinely accessible with future facilities such as LOFAR 2.0 and the Square Kilometre Array.

title: Reheating Constraints on the $α$-Starobinsky Model and Implications for Inflation Decays
summary: We constrain the $α$-Starobinsky model of inflation with an explicit reheating sector, in which the number of $e$-folds $N_*$ is computed for every sampled point from the reheating equation of state $w_{\mathrm{rh}}$ and temperature $T_{\mathrm{rh}}$, using a fully numerical pivot-scale matching in $\mathtt{CLASS}$. We analyze six combinations of Planck, Atacama Cosmology Telescope (ACT) DR6 and DESI DR2 baryon acoustic oscillation (BAO) data. The CMB sees reheating only through $\ln R_{\rm rad}\simeq N_*-N_{\rm inst}$, the shift of $N_*$ from its instantaneous-reheating value. At $α=1$, Planck gives $n_s=0.9656^{+0.0015}_{-0.0017}$ and is consistent with instantaneous reheating, $\ln R_{\rm rad}=0.4\pm2.7$. Planck, ACT and DESI together (P-ACT+DESI) give $n_s=0.9689^{+0.0012}_{-0.0016}$ and $\ln R_{\rm rad}=6.5^{+2.5}_{-3.1}$, which prefers a stiff phase ($w_{\mathrm{rh}}>0.47$ at 95$\%$). With $α$ free they give $\log_{10}α=1.0^{+0.5}_{-0.8}$, $n_s=0.9706^{+0.0016}_{-0.0020}$ and $\ln R_{\rm rad}=6^{+3}_{-4}$. This preference is not in agreement with the bound on the primordial gravitational-wave contribution. Imposing that bound approximately removes about half of the preferred stiff region. Comparing to an otherwise identical analysis in which $N_*$ is a free parameter, we find that the reheating sector acts mainly as a prior on $N_*$: at $α=1$ it narrows the inflationary posteriors, and with $α$ free it removes the largest values of $N_*$ and doubles the preferred $r$ for P-ACT+DESI. Finally, we briefly discuss the connection between these phenomenological constraints and representative perturbative inflaton decay scenarios, highlighting the limitations of this interpretation for stiff reheating histories.

title: One Prior, Two Dynamics: Repurposing Video Diffusion Transformers for Self-Supervised Latent Action Learning
summary: Videos reveal how the world changes, but rarely the actions that cause those changes. Latent action learning recovers such supervision from visual transitions, yet often learns the underlying dynamics largely from scratch. We ask whether a pretrained video generator can instead provide the prior for both inverse and forward dynamics. We introduce O$^{2}$LaF, built on a simple principle: one prior, two dynamics. We initialize both models from the same pretrained video DiT and adapt them to their distinct roles: a feed-forward transition encoder with learnable action queries for inverse dynamics, and a causal, action-conditioned video generator for forward dynamics. By controlling information access and optimizing both dynamics end-to-end through a compact bottleneck, O$^{2}$LaF learns transferable actions from unlabeled videos. Across navigation and robotic manipulation, O$^{2}$LaF sets a new state of the art in few-shot action probing and enables stronger zero-shot action transfer across visual contexts and embodiments. Beyond generative video priors, we further extend our framework to predictive representation priors such as V-JEPA2, achieving competitive performance. Our findings suggest a broader paradigm for latent-action learning: repurposing pretrained video models to discover transferable actions and predict their consequences.

title: BRUCE (Bayesian Rio Urban Climate Estimator): spatiotemporal interpolation of air temperature from heterogeneous sensor networks for operational heat monitoring
summary: Accurate characterization of intra-urban temperature variability is essential for heat-health surveillance, yet official monitoring networks are too sparse to resolve fine-scale gradients, particularly in Global South cities. We present BRUCE, a Bayesian hierarchical spatiotemporal model, fitted with the Integrated Nested Laplace Approximation (INLA) and a Stochastic Partial Differential Equation (SPDE) spatial component, that fuses four heterogeneous temperature sources for Rio de Janeiro, Brazil: official weather stations, low-cost IoT sensors, citizen-science personal weather stations and ERA5-Land reanalysis. The model accounts for class- and station-specific measurement bias and estimates a continuous spatial field that evolves day to day through an autoregressive (AR1) structure. Fitted independently to nine monthly windows (January, June, November; 2023--2025), the elevation coefficient was significant in all windows and of consistent magnitude in eight ($-$1.08 to $-$1.38 \textdegree{}C per SD). In leave-region-out cross-validation against LCZ4r, accuracy was comparable (RMSE differences within station-level bootstrap uncertainty in all three windows), while BRUCE produced predictions at every held-out station, including those where LCZ4r is masked, and preserved finer-scale spatial structure than LCZ4r's discrete zone classification. Applied to 241 primary care territories, BRUCE's posterior exceedance probabilities allowed 96 to be classified with high confidence (model-based classifications), whereas a constant-width interval derived from LCZ4r cross-validation errors supported confident classification of none. The framework offers a statistically principled, operationally viable basis for intra-urban heat monitoring in data-heterogeneous settings.

title: Field theory and the biquadratic spin-1 chain
summary: The antiferromagnetic biquadratic spin-1 chain is gapped, $SU(3)$ symmetric, and integrable. Standard arguments suggest that its low-energy physics is described by the $\mathbb{CP}^2$ nonlinear sigma model at $θ=π$. Using the Bethe ansatz, we show that its low-energy excitations can be interpreted as deconfined domain walls, just as in the sigma model. However, the lattice model is integrable, whereas the field theory is generally believed not to be. We propose a solution to this mystery by finding an integrable field theory with the same low-energy limit but which is not Lorentz invariant. The integrability-preserving scaling limit is obtained by adding a higher conserved charge and tuning the chain to criticality. The gap closes quadratically, so that the limit must be described by some nonrelativistic field theory rather than the relativistic sigma model. We describe the two-particle scattering matrix of this field theory.

title: Variants of Beam Search for DiskANN
summary: Graph-based data structures such as DiskANN, HNSW, and NSG constitute the state of the art for large-scale approximate nearest-neighbor (ANN) search. Indyk and Xu introduced the notion of $α$-reachable graphs, which include graphs built by DiskANN's slow-preprocessing construction, and proved that greedy search achieves an approximation factor of $\tfrac{α+1}{α-1}$. Independently, Al-Jazzazi et al. proposed adaptive beam search (ABS) with a relaxation parameter $γ> 0$, showing a $\tfrac{2}γ$ approximation on navigable graphs ($α\approx 1$), where greedy search admits no guarantees. In this work, we unify and generalize these results by proving that ABS with parameter $γ$ on $α$-reachable graphs achieves an approximation of $\tfrac{α+1}{α(γ+1)-1}$ for any metric. Moreover, on sorted $α$-reachable graphs (introduced by Gollapudi et al.) under the $\ell_2$ metric, we obtain the tighter bound $\max\bigl(\tfracα{α(γ+1)-1}, \tfrac{α^{2}+1}{α^{2}(γ+1)-1}\bigr)$. Beyond these theoretical results, we design a beam predictor using features inspired by fine-grained analysis of ABS, trained via a constrained objective that minimizes mean distance computations subject to a target recall. On three 100-million-point benchmarks, using graphs built by DiskANN's practical construction, beam predictor lowers mean query latency on SSD-resident indices at matched recall by up to $29.6\%$ relative to classical beam search (CBS). Relative to ABS, it is faster in $11$ of $15$ settings, by up to $6.5\%$, and at most $1.4\%$ slower in the other $4$; at $95\%$ recall, its advantage over ABS grows from $0.8$--$4.2\%$ for $100$ neighbors to $4.6$--$5.6\%$ for $500$ neighbors. In memory, it needs $1.3$--$23.7\%$ fewer distance computations than CBS and $0.0$--$3.9\%$ fewer than ABS.

title: Bio-PM-Guided Synthetic IMU Generation
summary: Collecting and labeling inertial measurement unit (IMU) data for human activity recognition (HAR) is expensive, and models trained on one group of subjects often fail to generalize to unseen individuals. Even with balanced data, classifiers struggle to distinguish dynamically similar activity classes and benefit from targeted augmentation. We explore whether synthetic IMU data generated in the representation space of a pretrained biosignal encoder, Bio-PM \cite{b1}, can serve as a practical augmentation source. Rather than synthesizing raw signals, we leverage Bio-PM's frozen encoder to convert 10-second IMU windows into token embedding sequences and train class-conditional decoders in this space: (1) an autoregressive transformer decoder that predicts tokens sequentially, and (2) a diffusion decoder that learns the token distribution through a denoising objective. We analyze generation realism through distributional metrics and embedding-space visualizations, evaluate downstream utility through leave-one-subject-out HAR classification, and present a PatchDecoder for approximate raw waveform reconstruction. Our diffusion decoder achieves a Train-on-Synthetic-Test-on-Real (TSTR) macro-F1 of 0.68, demonstrating that generated tokens are realistic enough to train a classifier that transfers to real data. Combining synthetic-token augmentation with a 320-dimensional gravity-aware feature representation raises LOSO macro-F1 from 0.729 to 0.809 over a real-only baseline across 51 subjects on the WISDM benchmark, with statistically significant gains concentrated in the most challenging activity classes. These results demonstrate that high-fidelity generation in a pretrained encoder's representation space is achievable and practically useful for cross-subject HAR augmentation.

title: SoK: Assessing the Evolution of LLM Capability in Software Vulnerability Research
summary: LLM-based agents are becoming increasingly capable at discovering, validating and patching vulnerabilities in real software, and vendors and researchers report that this is already changing how vulnerabilities are found and fixed. These claims, however, are scattered across papers, vendor reports and disclosures and are rarely comparable. We introduce a framework that rates these capabilities on an autonomy scale modeled on the levels of driving automation, and qualifies each claim by its correctness, its availability and the strength of its evidence. We use this framework to systematize the published evidence on LLM capability in vulnerability research. We find that agents discovered, validated, and patched vulnerabilities in real-world software without human intervention before the restricted frontier models of 2026, and that open-weight models subsequently attained comparable autonomy for discovery and validation. We then measure the consequences of evolving LLM security capabilities in a decade of public vulnerability records, advisories and exploitation data. In 2026 the number of disclosed vulnerabilities more than doubled, with an increasing share rated critical or high, and severe bugs that had survived a decade or more in widely used code were reported several times more often than before. Yet the time between the stages of a vulnerability's life, from report to fix and from disclosure to attack, has not shifted noticeably so far. We grade the mitigations proposed in the literature with an explicit rubric and draw guidance for each group of stakeholders from the best-supported ones.

title: PGX: Physically Grounded Execution for Long-Horizon Humanoid Loco-Manipulation
summary: Robotic vision-language-action (VLA) models can execute diverse individual manipulation skills, yet they still struggle with long-horizon loco-manipulation tasks, where temporal structure, skills, and precision are tightly coupled within a monolithic model. We propose Physically Grounded Execution (PGX), a framework that offloads temporal and precision control to two classical training-free components, allowing the VLA to focus on stage-specific skill dynamics. PGX decomposes long-horizon loco-manipulation into three layers: (i) a predicate-based state machine governs task progression, using physical predicates to gate phase transitions, trigger recovery, and coordinate navigation and waiting. Shared predicate semantics connect offline demonstration segmentation, online execution, and stage-wise evaluation; (ii) VLA skills operate within active manipulation phases, with flat or stage-trained models concentrating on task-relevant actions; and (iii) world-coordinate locking (WCL) maintains spatial consistency through base station keeping, object-relative positioning, and world-anchored contact targets. We demonstrate the effectiveness of PGX with extensive experiments conducted on three simulated tasks and one real-world task using a Unitree G1 humanoid robot for long-horizon loco-manipulation, showing improvements in stage progression and task success rates. Project page is available at: https://kl-research.github.io/pgx

title: UV Bounds on Inflationary Parity Violation
summary: A question of fundamental interest is whether parity is violated on large scales in the Universe. This possibility has been motivated by recent analyses of the four-point matter correlation function. It has also been suggested that detectable parity violation could be generated during inflation by the dynamical Chern-Simons operator, a leading effective field theory correction to general relativity. In this work, we examine this possibility in realistic UV completions, including fermionic and string-theoretic examples. We show that existing bounds on the tensor-scalar-scalar (TSS) bispectrum strongly constrain the possibility of generating a detectable parity-odd trispectrum. For tensor-to-scalar ratios near current observational limits, detectability is incompatible with, or pushes against, the regime of validity of these UV completions. A detectable signal can remain possible for a sufficiently small tensor-to-scalar ratio, but only at the cost of an extremely large enhancement of the TSS vertex. Thus, while a future search for large scale parity violation is worth pursuing, generating a detectable signal within a consistent effective theory is highly nontrivial.

title: Magnon high-harmonic generation by nonlinearities of spin torque driven by phonon-mediated crossing of many-body energy levels of bright and dark excitons
summary: Recent intense experimental focus on CrSBr, a two-dimensional (2D) antiferromagnetic semiconductor, has revealed numerous surprises in its response to ultrafast optical drive. We demonstrate that a single microscopic mechanism accounts for two of them---high-harmonic generation of magnons and persistence of magnon oscillations over \mbox{$\sim 1$ ns} time scale that is much longer than the femtosecond laser pulse (fsLP) pump duration. This mechanism arises from an unusually complex interplay of four different fundamental quasiparticles of condensed matter physics: magnons, optically bright and dark excitons, and phonons. By viewing magnons as the system and the other three quasiparticles as a quantum many-body bath, we derive an extended Landau-Lifshitz-Gilbert (eLLG) equation. Its new term generated by the bath is spatially nonlocal and time-dependent, as well as strongly {\em nonlinear} when the {\em crossing of many-body energy levels} of bright and dark excitons occurs via phonon mediation. It also resembles the so-called field-like spin-transfer torque (STT) in spintronics, but STT is driven there with current pulses, so it explains the microscopic origin of the recently experimentally conjectured {\em excitonic STT}. Since dark excitons supply energy to magnons long after the fsLP is switched off, such a reservoir opens avenues for its engineering and applications in optospintronics and optomagnonics, neuromorphic computing, and quantum transduction.

title: Verify the Verifier: Specification-Grounded LLM Cross-Checking for Bugs That Escape UVM Scoreboards
summary: A passing UVM regression shows the design agrees with the reference model on what the scoreboard checks, not that it meets the specification. Bugs that pass every test yet violate the specification, termed scoreboard escapes, survive mature testbenches. We present Verify the Verifier, to our knowledge the first framework whose LLM-based Anomaly Cross-Checker examines a passing regression's traces against the specification. Of 564 bugs inserted into four OpenTitan IPs, 68 are candidate scoreboard escapes: non-equivalent, exercised by the tests, yet passing. The framework confirmed 41 as scoreboard escapes with assertions failing on the buggy design and proven on the original.

title: Puzzles, People, and Publications: Measuring Shared Significance in Crosswords from 1942 to 2024
summary: Crossword puzzles are cultural objects that encode shared significance. We use interpretable, large-scale computational methods to analyze how crossword constructors, editors, and publications have adopted and adapted language to convey significance. Focusing on approximately 2.4 million crossword clue/answer pairs published in The New York Times between 1942 and 2024, we find shifting significance and differing editorial practices to be quantitatively measurable. By computationally measuring shared significance over time in crossword puzzle production, we are able to better understand cultural changes in the United States through the 20th and early 21st centuries.

title: End-to-End Quantum Algorithm for Differential Equations: Application to Simulating a Biomolecular System
summary: Quantum algorithms for differential equations have the potential for substantial algorithmic speedups over classical methods. However, they rely on certain assumptions and abstract oracle specifications that leave their practical feasibility and computational advantages for realistic applications unclear. Here we formalize the concept of an end-to-end quantum algorithm for differential equations as one that accepts classical inputs and returns classical outputs, and provide implementations for algorithmic primitives in constructing such algorithms. We present a tailored end-to-end quantum algorithm for the linearized Poisson-Boltzmann (LPB) equation, a partial differential equation (PDE) with variable coefficients widely used in simulating a biomolecular system. We explicitly implement all aspects of the algorithm, from preparing an initial state to generating a quantum solution and estimating properties of the system. In particular, we develop a new discrete representation for variable-coefficient PDEs on a grid that enables efficient implementation of the operator oracle, and build on a recent technique based on optimal wavelet preconditioning to generate a quantum solution with a cost independent of the condition number of the discretized operator. We show the algorithm can be implemented by quantum circuits of size polylogarithmic in both the number of grid points $N_g$ and the inverse of the desired accuracy $\varepsilon$, with an overall gate cost polylogarithmic in $N_g$ and quasilinear in $1/\varepsilon$. We also show the classical preprocessing to construct the circuits has polylogarithmic cost in $N_g$ and $1/\varepsilon$. Our work provides a concrete end-to-end quantum algorithm for a PDE of practical value, demonstrates an exponential improvement in scaling with $N_g$ over classical methods, and provides a foundation for assessing its potential quantum advantage in practice.

title: Classically Trained Quantum Generative Models with Shared Training and Fine Tuning for Quantum Matter
summary: Ground-state measurement statistics characterize quantum matter. Selected correlations can guide the classical training of a quantum sampler even when sampling the full distribution is difficult. We ask whether training across related ground-state distributions helps the sampler reproduce their correlations more accurately. We train a hypernetwork to map Hamiltonian parameters to circuit angles, sharing information across the phase diagram before local fine-tuning with additional reference data for quantum deployment. For classical training, we derive an unbiased Monte Carlo estimator of Fourier coefficients for circuits built from general Pauli rotations, with a cost that depends on the circuit generators. We also introduce a CDF-KL loss for comparing selected marginals. We study the Haldane Hamiltonian and transverse-field Ising model, using an automated search to select reference calculations near phase transitions. On the twelve-site chain, the adaptively pretrained hypernetwork matches the independent fits' final mean total variation distance in fewer local updates and continues to a lower error. On a 1,024-site chain and a 4 by 256 lattice, the fine-tuned circuits have lower squared maximum mean discrepancy from the reference distributions than the independent circuits at the evaluated point in each geometry. These results motivate shared training for preparing quantum samplers across a phase diagram and local fine-tuning.

title: Modeling the gravitational wave spectrum from slowly-evolving sources in the early Universe: constant-in-time and coherent-decay models
summary: We study the production of gravitational wave (GW) backgrounds from slowly-evolving sources in the early Universe, following the Constant-in-Time (CiT) model, presented and validated against simulations of decaying turbulence in arXiv:2201.05630. We extend the CiT model to account for the source decay using a coherent description for the unequal-time correlator (UETC) of the source. We present a generic framework that allows us to study different types of sources. As examples, we discuss the applicability of this framework to the production of GWs from decaying MHD turbulence, sound waves, and bubble collisions in first-order phase transitions. We show that the validity of the CiT and the coherent-decay models presented in this work relies on long decorrelation times of the source. However, as the decorrelation timescale of the UETC becomes short, a resonant term grows on top of the GW spectrum predicted by the CiT model, as found, for example, in earlier analytical studies of GW production from turbulence and sound waves. This model is compatible with previous numerical results and explains why sound waves in a radiation-dominated fluid are more efficient than subrelativistic MHD turbulence in producing GWs, which is no longer the case for relativistic turbulence. The CiT model predicts a generic spectrum that scales as $k^3$ in the IR regime, develops a linear $k$ at intermediate frequencies, and decays as $k^{1-b_Π}$ at frequencies above the inverse correlation length scale of the source, where $b_Π$ is uniquely determined by the type of source and the UV slope of its spectrum. Since the $k^3$ and $k$ scalings always appear for slowly-evolving sources and they are commonly found in studies of GW production, we motivate checking the potential applicability of the CiT to other sources of GWs.

title: Irreducible Governance Structure for Autonomous Agent Systems: Fair Allocation, Strategy-Proofness, and Multi-Scale Composition
summary:
Autonomous agent governance is commonly framed as a problem of enforcing correct execution. However, in multi-agent systems, an equally fundamental question precedes execution: which agents are allowed to act.
  In this paper, we show that allocation is not an auxiliary concern but a structural component of governance. When multiple agents compete for execution under constrained resources, any allocation mechanism introduces unavoidable trade-offs between fairness, efficiency, and resistance to strategic manipulation. We formalize this through a set of impossibility results, including Sybil amplification and the incompatibility of desirable allocation properties.
  We then show that these allocation constraints cannot be resolved within a single layer of control. Instead, they propagate across the system, interacting with execution atomicity, state enforcement, and behavioral drift. This leads to a multi-scale governance structure composed of four orthogonal dimensions: temporal (atomicity), state (enforcement), behavioral (drift monitoring), and population (allocation).
  Our main result is an irreducibility theorem: under finite observability, no governance architecture can collapse these dimensions without loss of correctness or stability. Allocation, in particular, acts as a first-class constraint that prevents simplification of the governance stack.
  We validate these results through a series of analytical constructions and empirical ablations, showing that removing or approximating any layer leads to systematic failure modes.
  This work reframes agent governance as a structural problem: not only how actions are executed, but how access to execution is determined, and why these decisions impose irreducible architectural requirements.

title: STEGOGUARD-LM: Evaluating End-to-End Protection Against LLM Covert Channels
summary: A defense that disrupts hidden messages may still provide little protection if its detector rarely triggers an intervention. We present StegoGuard-LM, a controlled framework for evaluating defenses against covert messages in large language model outputs. We examine token-rank and synonym channels, with Unicode concealment as a structural control, and track messages through detection, intervention, and recovery. Deterministic rewriting prevented full recovery of 103 of 104 synonym-encoded messages when applied unconditionally, but only one when intervention depended on a detector set to limit false alarms. In a four-round replay on a 48-response subset, an attacker selecting from a fixed catalog recovered more bits by switching channels, although paired gains were not statistically significant after correction for multiple comparisons. Randomized rewriting showed no sustained advantage in this pilot. A more sensitive detector improved protection but modified about one-third of clean responses. These findings show how uneven detection can undermine effective rewriting and why protection must be evaluated alongside attacker adaptation and intervention on legitimate text.

title: Neighbourhood Walkability and Cardiometabolic Morbidity in Greater London: A Fine-Grained Spatial Analysis
summary: Cardiometabolic diseases are leading causes of ill health, and neighbourhoods that support everyday walking may help reduce them. Studies often report lower disease prevalence in more walkable neighbourhoods. However, because walkability operates across multiple spatial scales, city-wide associations may conflate local neighbourhood form with broader metropolitan structure and co-varying environmental exposures. Here we show that while much of the walkability--morbidity association in Greater London operates through the city's macro-scale spatial structure, local alignment persists beyond it. Using an open five-component walkability index for 4,994 London census units and recorded prevalence of eight cardiometabolic conditions from primary-care registers, we found that higher walkability was inversely associated with all eight outcomes after adjusting for demographic composition and deprivation; one standard deviation higher walkability corresponded to 1.43 percentage points lower hypertension prevalence. Walkability followed a centre--periphery gradient, with a radial model explaining 74.2\% of its variation. Coefficients were reduced by 2--43\% within boroughs and 11--75\% after centre--periphery adjustment. After spatial-error adjustment, no clear association remained for obesity; coefficients for the other seven were reduced by 83--99\% relative to comparable log-scale models. Nevertheless, observed associations were more extreme than those from surrogate walkability surfaces preserving this spatial structure, for all eight outcomes in the primary analyses and for five after adjustment for nitrogen oxides. These findings caution against interpreting city-wide walkability coefficients as neighbourhood effects independent of wider metropolitan structure, and highlight the need for studies of neighbourhood form and health to disentangle global and local spatial structure explicitly.

title: PhyDEX: A Benchmark for Physical Reasoning in Vision-Language-Action Models via Dynamic Extrinsic Dexterity
summary: Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models have advanced rapidly in language-conditioned robotic manipulation, yet existing benchmarks mainly evaluate gripper--object contact and largely ignore how objects interact with the environment through gravity, friction, inertia, and mass distribution. As a result, it remains unclear whether current policies truly understand physics or merely interpolate from their training data. We address this gap through the lens of dynamic extrinsic dexterity and introduce PhyDEX, a throwing benchmark in which a robot must infer an object's mass, center of mass, and friction to send it to a destination beyond its kinematic workspace. PhyDEX contains 35K trajectories (143 hours) across nine tasks and 100 scenes, covering uniform, irregular, and dynamic-mass objects with static, multiple, and moving destinations. All data are generated by a scalable, fully automatic pipeline that combines grasp generation, motion planning, and closed-loop throw optimization under randomized physical properties. We evaluate three representative VLAs, GR00T N1.7, DynamicVLA, and ForceVLA, and find that all achieve success rates below 3\%. Our analysis reveals two key bottlenecks: limited robustness of pretrained models, which causes most failures before the throw, and physical blindness, as providing ground-truth physical properties roughly doubles success. Experiments on a humanoid robot and in the real world show the same failure patterns. We hope PhyDEX will drive the development of physically grounded robot policies.

title: Replication of Agentic Security Events: Audit and Investigation (ROGUE-AI)
summary: Agents based on large language models (LLMs) can now delete files and send payments on behalf of their users. News media reports routinely describe failures of these agents (e.g., Replit's coding agent deleting a production database), but a report often only says what went wrong and rarely (in)validates the incident or finds its root cause. Incident catalogs collect these reports, and benchmarks record whether agents fail, but neither replicates an incident nor tests the cause its report might identify. In this paper, we present ROGUE-AI (Replication of Agentic Security Events: Audit and Investigation), a multi-agent framework that closes the above gap and rebuilds each reported incident offline together with a matched control that lacks only the blamed cause, and runs agents on both. Our results suggest that ROGUE-AI is able to reproduce the reported harm in 89% of its 108 attempted replications. Agents built on five current GPT, Claude, Gemini and DeepSeek models made the reported mistake in 18% to 33% of runs, against at most 1% without the blamed cause. Of the 72 incidents with real-world harm, 62 had no underlying attacker, and in these, agents did what their task asked for but missed an ordinary hazard, such as a database shared with the live site. Replications without an attacker caused more harm than replications of prompt injection for all five models. Defenses against prompt injection look for injected instructions, but these replications contain none. Further, a warning after each tool output that names the hazard and its consequence lowered harm for all five models, whereas a note of the same length that does not mention the hazard left most of the harm in place. Built from real incidents, the ROGUE-AI replications form a reusable audit framework that vendors can rerun before each new release.

title: GraphEP: A Calibrated Data System and Benchmark for Learning Cardiac Electrophysiology
summary: High-fidelity simulations generate spatiotemporal data that are difficult to obtain experimentally, yet their outputs are rarely ready for scientific machine learning. Cardiac electrophysiology (EP) exemplifies this challenge: data reside on anatomy-dependent volumetric meshes, propagation follows anisotropic material fields, and relevant events span multiple temporal scales. We introduce GraphEP, a calibrated data system that converts cardiac meshes and simulation protocols into compact, graph-native trajectories of full-field transmembrane potential. GraphEP includes 732 left-ventricular simulations across 20 anatomies, with healthy and scarred substrates of varying severity and multiple pacing configurations. Each sample provides geometry, tissue and material features, stimulation, connectivity, derived activation targets, and provenance in PyTorch Geometric format. We benchmark four inductive biases for predicting transmembrane potential Vm(t): local message passing, global neural operators, multi-scale hierarchical graph transformers (HGT), and physiology-informed models. The latter include HGT-Lag, which separates activation timing from action-potential morphology, and the stateful Graph Aliev-Panfilov Action-Potential ODE (GAP2ODE), which evolves excitation and recovery autoregressively with frame-wise stimulation and graph diffusion. Results show that wider spatial communication improves on local message passing, while physiological structure provides the strongest inductive bias: HGT-Lag and GAP2ODE lead on complementary metrics by explicitly modeling propagation, recovery, and temporal state. GraphEP offers a reproducible pathway from mechanistic cardiac EP simulations to analysis-ready data and a controlled benchmark for learning on irregular anatomical geometries.

title: Chemical Cartography Across Time: The Age-Dependent Chemical Structure of the Milky Way with a Homogeneous Sample of 580,000 Giants from Five Surveys
summary: Mapping the distribution of elements in the Milky Way and understanding how that distribution has changed over time can give us insight into the formation and evolution of our Galaxy. Here we use homogeneously estimated atmospheric parameters, elemental abundances, distances, and ages for ~580,000 giants from five major spectroscopic surveys---all simultaneously placed on a single, self-consistent scale by one model---allowing us, for the first time, to use a large sample of stars with uniform labels and ages that cumulatively span much of the disk to trace how the metallicity structure of the Milky Way depends on stellar age. Our chrono-chemical analysis shows that the radial metallicity gradient of the disk depends non-monotonically on age: it is shallow for the youngest stars, steepening to a maximum of ~-0.07 dex/kpc at intermediate ages (~5-6 Gyr), and flattening to near zero for the oldest stars. This "U-shaped" age dependence is driven largely by the low-alpha (thin-disk) population, with the high-alpha (thick-disk) sequence having weak gradients at all ages. In contrast to [Fe/H], the radial [Mg/Fe] gradient is weak (<~0.01 dex/kpc) at all ages. Together, these trends are consistent with an inside-out formation scenario in which the gradient of the star-forming gas has flattened over at least the last ~6 Gyr, while the near-zero gradient of the oldest stars reflects their formation in a well-mixed disk, efficient radial migration, or both.

title: The Geometry of Lies: Knowledge and Persona Directions for Detecting Deception in Large Language Models
summary: Linear probes are the cheapest LLM lie detectors but often fail to transfer across kinds of lie. Label-free directions from honest and deceptive role-play are untested at 70B scale and on lies about knowledge, where a lie and an honest denial can be identical. We widen a published persona bank with roles that deny knowledge they have, plus honest counterparts. At each model's middle layer the resulting persona direction ranks lies across Liars' Bench better than single-dataset probes on three of its four models; it fails on Qwen, even when Qwen stays in role far more often. On Llama-3.3-70B-Instruct it beats directions from a random persona bank, but its gain over the published direction is within the range of random widenings. On lies about knowledge, persona directions mainly track a reply's wording: where lies and honest denials share their words, our three main contrasts stay inside the random-direction band on Llama and Qwen and reach only its edge on Gemma, though on Mistral one clears it. A knowledge direction contrasts questions the model can answer with ones nobody can, each followed by the same scripted denial. It separates lies from identical honest denials on two models and narrowly on a third, but not on the fourth; its other results partly depend on the benchmark's wording. On the Gender-Secret fine-tune it clears the band by a few hundredths on Llama and fails on Mistral. The sum of the two directions ranks lies better than a supervised probe at the same depth on all four models (on one, both near chance) but is level with the persona direction on Llama's average and behind that probe on held-out lies. More varied role-play questions do not help the persona direction on Liars' Bench.

title: LLM GerryMandering: Separating Interactions from Additive Effects in LLM Audits
summary: Intersectional bias arises when a model treats people who hold several marginalised identities at once differently from what their separate identities would predict. Auditing such intersectional subgroups remains a challenge: their number grows quadratically, and there is no agreed baseline for what independent attributes would predict. Without such a baseline, many existing audits flag a subgroup when it exceeds each attribute alone, a condition that attributes acting independently already satisfy. We test this standard criterion on 150 synthetic datasets built with no interaction. With the shuffle null, it flags 66.1 false subgroups per dataset on average, and at least one in every dataset. When we plant interactions of known size into these datasets, a repaired null lets the criterion recover only 32% of them. We introduce ADDIS (Additive Intersectional Screen), which fits an additive model over all attributes, scores each subgroup by its Additive Residual Distance (ARD) from that model's prediction, and tests it against a Freedman-Lane null. On our synthetic benchmark, ADDIS flags 0.09 false subgroups per dataset and recovers 84% of the same planted interactions. We then build IndiPersona, 10,000 synthetic Indian personas with six identity attributes, and audit 13 open language models. The standard criterion flags 7.1% of the 738 tested subgroups on average; ADDIS flags 3.0%. Gender identity crossed with sexual orientation is the largest pairing in every model, and counterfactual personas confirm it and additionally reveal a caste x class interaction in all but one model that the observational test lacked the data to detect. Much of what audits report as intersectional bias can thus arise from independent single-attribute effects alone, yet a small core of interactions survives.

title: Emergent Fatigue Dynamics from Foundational Interatomic Potentials
summary: Foundational machine-learned interatomic potentials are trained on large, diverse DFT datasets, but their validation rests on equilibrium states, which does not guarantee correct emergent behavior in large-scale molecular dynamics. Where no direct experimental validation is available, comparisons to physically motivated potentials are valuable for drawing insight. We distinguish static properties, which are thermally accessible, from emergent properties, which require work from an external fatigue stress to drive rare events, and compare the potentials on both. An EAM potential and the NequIP foundational potential both agree closely with reference data for many near-equilibrium properties, but NequIP predicts an anomalously low intrinsic stacking fault energy ($\sim7$ times lower than EAM) and thus predicts far more plastic deformation under fatigue cycling of a nanoscale flaw modeled after the classical Griffith crack problem. Per-atom energy distributions after loading show that the two potentials differ most at energies far above what is thermally accessible. We also document memory-related crashes and silent extrapolation as practical concerns for practitioners of these foundational model forms.

title: Cost-Aware Agentic Feature Optimization System for Fleet-Scale Ranking Models
summary: Large Web platforms operate large fleets of ranking models, each selecting features from a shared pool of tens of thousands. We present an end-to-end agentic system that optimizes features across the fleet under resource constraints shared across models and those set per model, such as feature pipeline cost and serving throughput (QPS), respectively. In this system, LLM agents propose hypotheses, and deterministic tools execute experiments and verify them. For each model, an LLM generates and shortlists cross features from a combinatorial candidate space, and all features are then ranked by several importance methods. Feature blending mixes these rankings into a single selection, using Pareto fronts across tasks for multi-task models. An LLM Researcher agent then tunes the feature selection in 10--25 asynchronous trials under resource caps, and a trimming step keeps the pipeline cost within budget. Across production models, the system improves normalized entropy by 0.31% on average within each model's budget, and the trimming step cuts pipeline cost by 2.3% with no regression beyond measurement noise. The optimized models were launched, and in online A/B tests they improved a primary online metric by 0.20%.

title: Exact fermionic decay length and Majorana localization in the sign-alternating kagomé Ising model
summary: We derive an exact fermionic decay length for the sign-alternating kagomé Ising model at fixed transverse momentum $p=π/2$. Writing $x=\tanh K_1$, $y=\tanh K_2$, and $z=\tanh K_3$ for the three dimensionless couplings, the inverse length per lattice cell is $ξ_{\rm f}^{-1}=|\ln(U/|V|)|$, where $U=(1-x^2)(1+y^2z^2)$ and $V=(1+x^2)(y^2-z^2)$. The length diverges at $U=|V|$, with the sign of $V$ selecting one of two classical critical branches. In a simultaneous strong- and weak-bond scaling, these branches become the gap-closing conditions at momenta $0$ and $π$ of the transverse-field Ising chain obtained from the row transfer matrix. On the topological side, the classical decay length tends to the localization length of a Majorana end mode of the Jordan--Wigner fermion chain. We also prove that the regular strong-bond Yang--Baxter family cannot be continued to the finite-coupling interior within the fixed-basis ansatz with one vanishing bond direction.

title: Thermal-Guided Ensemble Reinforcement Learning for Regime-Adaptive Short-Term GPU Power Forecasting in AI Data Centers
summary: AI data centers (AIDCs) introduce bursty and regime-dependent load patterns, posing significant challenges for reliable energy management and predictive grid control. To address these challenges, this letter proposes a thermal-guided ensemble reinforcement learning framework for probabilistic AIDC load forecasting. A soft actor-critic (SAC) agent with a simplex-preserving policy adaptively weights LSTM, TCN, and Transformer predictors at every time step based on their realized errors. A thermal-guided neural correction estimates the ensemble residual, while a sensitivity-projection regularizer enforces the non-negative sensitivity of power to GPU utilization and temperature. The corrected ensemble output is further processed by a Bayesian probabilistic layer to produce predictive distributions and quantify forecasting uncertainty. Case studies on 1-second MIT Supercloud telemetry show that the proposed method reduces the normalized mean absolute error to about 1% across all computing regimes, compared with 4-11% for deep learning-based and ensemble learning benchmarks, and converges faster with narrower prediction intervals than a DRL ensemble without thermal guidance.

title: Hamiltonian Stabilization of the Two-Photon Dicke Model
summary: Collective two-photon light--matter interactions enable pair amplification but can destroy spectral confinement, preventing a stable thermodynamic bright phase. We show that a positive Kac-scaled number-Kerr interaction renders the two-photon Dicke Hamiltonian of \(N\) emitters lower-bounded at all couplings while preserving its generalized \(\mathbb Z_4\) symmetry. We determine the exact zero-temperature thermodynamic energy density with \(O(N^{-1})\) finite-size control and obtain the global phase diagram. A bright minimum is born at a saddle-node and exchanges global stability with the normal minimum at coexistence, producing a discontinuous photon-density jump. Symmetry-resolved exact diagonalization through \(N=128\) supports the predicted density jump and an exponentially closing same-sector normal--bright tunneling gap. Spectral collapse thus becomes the singular zero-Kerr point of a first-order phase diagram, identifying a Hamiltonian route to stabilizing pair amplification.

title: $Zγ$ production in gluon fusion at NLO+NLL
summary: We study the production of $Zγ$ in gluon fusion at hadron colliders at the next-to-leading-order (NLO) in QCD. At the $13.6$ TeV LHC, we find that these NLO corrections are found to enhance the leading-order (LO) cross section by about $83$\% and reduce the conventional seven-point scale uncertainty from $22.3$\% at LO to $15.2$\% at NLO. We further perform the threshold resummation at next-to-leading-logarithmic (NLL) accuracy and match to the fixed order NLO results. We have presented the production cross section for various center of mass energies at the LHC. We find that this NLL resummation enhances the NLO production cross section by about $23$\%. We also give the invariant mass distribution up to $Q=1000$ GeV for $13.6$ TeV LHC. In this case, the resummation reduces the seven-point scale uncertainty from $25\%$ at NLO to about $16$\% at NLO+NLL for $Q=1000$ GeV. We also present the uncertainties due to the strong coupling constant and the parton distribution functions in our results. We further estimate the contribution of the top quark in our predictions, using the Born Improved Theory (BIT).

title: From Seed to BLOOM: Autonomously Growing a Better Out-of-Order Core
summary:
Improving microprocessor performance while meeting ASIC implementation constraints like area and frequency is a complex and labor-intensive task that requires expertise across computer architecture, hardware design, and performance analysis and profiling. While large teams in industry can afford the engineering resources to target this problem across performance modeling, RTL design, and ASIC implementations, small teams of researchers and engineers cannot take on this huge engineering burden while keeping up with the pace of advancement in processor microarchitecture. Recent advancements in large language model (LLM) agents present a promising substrate to accelerate this traditionally human-intensive process.
  In this work, we build and evaluate MiracleGro, an agentic AI-based system that, without human intervention, analyzes cycle-level RTL behavior and synthesis results, identifies performance bottlenecks, and translates architectural ideas into RTL implementation in a leading open-source out-of-order superscalar application core, the Berkeley Out-of-Order Machine (BOOM). Taking into account cycle-exact performance, area, and critical path, MiracleGro automatically produces improved BOOM designs that drastically increase the human-optimized BOOM's performance on substantial workload suites such as SPEC CPU2017 with full reference inputs.
  MiracleGro achieves an 85% IPC speedup and a frequency improvement of 27% in SkyWater 130nm, resulting in a 2.34x wall-clock time speedup on the full SPEC CPU2017 intspeed benchmarks (30 trillion instructions). This result demonstrates the enormous opportunity to harness frontier models to improve state-of-the-art RTL-driven platforms for implementation-grounded microarchitecture research across hardware designs.

title: AutoMaster: Autonomous Post-Training by Making the Same Model a Better Teacher
summary: Task success alone does not specify which behaviors post-training should reinforce. Even successful teacher trajectories can contain unsupported assumptions, unproductive repetition, or superficial verification. We propose Skill-FT (Skill-Guided Fine-Tuning), which uses natural-language skills to suppress undesirable habits and elicit underrepresented effective behaviors during teacher rollouts, then fine-tunes a target model on the resulting trajectories. We introduce AutoMaster, an autonomous post-training system in which an LLM agent develops these interventions through trajectory analysis, skill design, data selection, and feedback from rollouts and target-model evaluation. Across Terminal, Search, and software engineering tasks with 4B and 9B target models, AutoMaster improves mean performance over Vanilla SFT on successful unguided teacher trajectories by 1.42-8.99 percentage points, with the teacher, task pool, training set size, and SFT recipe held fixed. Together with the ablations and trajectory analyses, these results suggest that behavioral shaping can make a fixed model a more effective teacher. We further find that retaining skill instructions during SFT yields higher mean performance than removing them across all six settings, despite their absence at evaluation and identical supervised outputs. These findings suggest that preserving skill context as part of a training demonstration can support better behavioral internalization.

title: Grid Cells as Spectral Successor Features: A Reusable Basis for Continual Reinforcement Learning
summary: Continual reinforcement learning requires agents to adapt when the task changes while reusing what they know about the environment. Successor features separate dynamics from task-specific reward, but their effectiveness depends on the choice of base features. Taking the identification of entorhinal grid cells with eigenvectors of the successor representation as a design principle, we build this basis from eigenvectors of the transition matrix of a fixed reference policy. With such a basis, the successor features at a state-action pair are a linear combination of the base features at that same pair, which is not true in general, and the coefficients are known in closed form: each successor feature is its base feature multiplied by $θ_i = 1/(1-γλ_i)$, where $λ_i$ is its eigenvalue. The long-term return is thus predicted from the same features as the immediate reward, no successor-feature network or replay buffer is needed, and adapting to a new task reduces to a linear regression on the reward. The agent acts greedily on the action values of the reference policy, which is one step of policy improvement over it and suffices to reach a single goal. In a two-goal gridworld, with the uniform random walk as reference policy, whose eigenvectors are the low-frequency Laplacian eigenvectors, agents built this way maintain near-maximal return across every change of goal, whereas SimpleSF and DQN lose most of their return at each change.

title: Existence and uniqueness for a coagulation-transport equation
summary: This paper establishes the existence, uniqueness, and regularity of weak solutions to a class of nonlinear coagulation-transport equations describing the asymptotic dynamics of multispecies coalescent processes. The model captures the multi-scale ancestral lineage decay governed by an autonomous drift field, coupled with a time-inhomogeneous quadratic coagulation term parameterized by the initial population mass. By utilizing the metric structure of probability measures, we demonstrate that any weak solution satisfies a unique mild representation formula dictated by the transport semigroup. This characterization allows us to construct a unified narrative where existence, uniqueness, and moment preservation are proved directly through a contractive fixed-point argument in the space of finite Radon measures.

title: Optimal Error corrected Hamiltonian estimation with nuisance parameters
summary: Realistic quantum sensing is often affected by both noise and unknown nuisance parameters. Under Markovian dynamics, existing error correction approaches have often sought to suppress nuisance responses alongside environmental noise. Here we show that this local suppression of nuisance parameters is unnecessary and can be overly restrictive: nuisance parameters and Markovian noise impose fundamentally different constraints and require distinct treatments. We establish a general framework for quantum sensing with parameters encoded in a general time dependent Hamiltonian, in the presence of both nuisance parameters and Markovian noise. We derive a necessary and sufficient condition for Heisenberg scaling, determine the exact optimal precision, and construct protocols that attain it. Our results show that to achieve Heisenberg scaling Markovian noise must be suppressed locally by quantum error correction, whereas nuisance parameters need not, and in general should not, be eliminated locally. Instead, optimally designed coherent control can separate their accumulated effects from the target signal over the full sensing evolution. Consequently, Heisenberg scaling can remain attainable even when the target signal is instantaneously aligned with nuisance parameter directions, in sharp contrast to alignment with Markovian noise. This distinction substantially enlarges the regime in which Heisenberg scaling is attainable and provides a general principle for designing robust quantum sensors.

title: Inhomogeneous Cutoff Regularization of Loops in Cosmological Correlators
summary: We revisit the use of cutoff regularization in computing loop corrections to cosmological correlators. We argue that a cutoff corresponding to a fixed physical scale must be defined with respect to the local background geometry. In the presence of superhorizon perturbations, this is naturally implemented within the separate universe picture, where different local patches are regulated at the same physical scale. Expanding this cutoff in the long-wavelength background generates a series of regulator-induced contributions to loop amplitudes, which admit a diagrammatic interpretation as long-mode insertions on the corresponding loop contractions. Our cutoff prescription preserves residual spatial dilatations and volume-preserving anisotropic rescalings. It is therefore particularly relevant for loop correlators with soft external modes. We illustrate the mechanism by computing the contributions to the one-loop scalar and tensor power spectra on superhorizon scales. In both cases, the additional corrections induced by the inhomogeneous cutoff cancel the ultraviolet boundary terms arising in the ordinary diagrams. These calculations establish, within cutoff regularization, the late-time constancy of both power spectra and clarify its physical origin. We then investigate the squeezed one-loop scalar bispectrum and show that the additional cutoff contributions are essential for satisfying the consistency relation at finite cutoff. Finally, we discuss the role of the inhomogeneous cutoff in the late-time constancy of the one-loop bispectrum.

title: SGAR: Feed-Forward 3D Reconstruction via Sparse Geometry-Guided Attention
summary: Feed-forward models have been very successful in 3D reconstruction with ad hoc attention designs that relate all view patches densely. However, the cost of this dense global attention grows quadratically with the number of views, preventing the model from applying to larger-scale reconstruction settings. In this paper, we argue that most dense attention computations are unnecessary from a classical structure-from-motion perspective: 3D structures stem from geometrically matching regions in 2D. We bring this principle to learning-based feed-forward reconstruction with our Sparse Geometric Attention Reconstruction (SGAR) method. In SGAR, each patch token attends to only a small set of patch tokens from other views, chosen by a lightweight learned key selection module trained to predict cross-view 3D proximity of tokens. Thus, dense global attention is replaced by much more efficient geometric-similarity-guided sparse attention. SGAR is a general method that can be applied to different feed-forward models by fine-tuning. In our experiments, we show that SGAR is the fastest among both state-of-the-art dense and sparse methods and the most accurate sparse one. It runs up to 12-times faster than dense attention at 1,000 views with stable pose accuracy where existing sparse methods fail, and shows the best performance in reconstructing more complete geometries on the same time budget.

title: Multimodal Error Detection in Chest X-ray Reports: A Large Language Model Reading Image Evidence
summary: Rad-Linter checks chest X-ray reports against image-derived evidence to flag potential errors for review. A pretrained image classifier supplies scores for nine pathologies, and a 1.5B-parameter language model, fine-tuned with LoRA on 1,816 examples, checks their consistency with the report. We compare it with a keyword-and-negation rule baseline given the same reports and scores. Evaluation uses controlled report-score pairings from OpenI, with consistency labels derived from automatic report labels and score thresholds. Each counterfactual quad crosses two real reports with two real score vectors from other patients, creating two consistent and two inconsistent pairs. Every report and score vector occurs in both conditions, so either input alone permits only 50% accuracy. On 131 quads, Rad-Linter achieves 98.5% pair accuracy versus 80.5% for the rule baseline, and classifies all four pairs correctly in 94.4% of quads versus 56.5%. The checkers perform similarly on omission items, including unmentioned and negated findings; larger differences occur on the remaining item types, which require interpreting how findings are described. The same language model without fine-tuning remains near 50% accuracy. On a second set of 181 quads that also includes reports on which the automatic labelers disagree, pair accuracy is 93.4% versus 75.3%. These controlled results show that, given the same image-derived scores, a trained language model detects report-score inconsistencies more accurately than the tested rule baseline, with the advantage concentrated in interpreting how findings are worded.

title: Spatiotemporal Risk-Based Hotspot Dynamics Assessment
summary: Analysis of hotspots often constitutes the final objective in application studies oriented to spatiotemporal risk assessment, particularly for risk mapping and as a helpful instrument for decision making, in diverse fields such as Ecology, Epidemiology, Environmental Sciences, Security, among others. The most primary form, common in practice, consists in identifying and depicting the areas where the magnitude of interest exceeds a certain critical threshold level. In this work, we introduce a wider, more general concept of `hotspot', associated with the extremal values of risk measures defined on different structural indicators of threshold exceedance sets, such as the exceedance area, the excess volume, etc. In particular, we propose a methodological approach based on empirical characterization of the indicator probability distributions from simulation conditional on the available observations, calculated at local resolution scales determined by sliding windows. Risk map generation is then supported by a proper conceptualization and formalization of a suitable family of risk conditional random fields (RCRFs), specified in terms of a set of input elements that can be viewed as flexible tuning parameters for practical implementation and application. For illustration, we consider an extension of a spatiotemporal diffusive blur-generated autoregressive model involving a dynamical spatial deformation. Evolutionary assessment of hotspots is then addressed under different scenarios, with reference to well-known quantile-based risk measures.

title: Constraints and biases: impact of light-cone effects on power spectrum and bispectrum forecasts
summary: Next-generation galaxy surveys will map large-scale structure over unprecedented volumes, bringing two goals within reach: constraining primordial non-Gaussianity (PNG) and detecting relativistic effects on the largest scales. On these scales, relativistic and wide-separation (light-cone) effects share the scale dependence of local-type PNG, so they must be modelled to avoid biased inferences and to recover the true uncertainties. We present joint power spectrum and bispectrum forecasts that include these effects, with a multi-tracer bispectrum covariance including the odd-parity multipoles and leading non-Gaussian terms. Neglecting light-cone effects biases local-type $f_{\rm NL}$ by $\sim2σ$ for a Euclid-like H$α$ survey and $>10σ$ for a MegaMapper-like LBG survey, mostly through lensing; wide-separation and local relativistic effects contribute $<1σ$. With these corrections included, marginalising over the evolution and magnification biases without informative priors increases the uncertainty on local-type $f_{\rm NL}$ by $\sim60\%$ for a Euclid-like power spectrum and by $\sim50\%$ for a joint power spectrum and bispectrum analysis of the even multipoles. However, the odd-parity multipoles of the single-tracer bispectrum and the multi-tracer power spectrum, which are sensitive to leading-order relativistic corrections, break most of this degeneracy. Non-local shapes are less affected; for these, a bright-faint split of the MegaMapper-like survey improves the joint constraints on the equilateral and orthogonal shapes by a factor of $\sim2$. Finally, local relativistic effects should be detectable at SNR $\sim13$, with a bright-faint split of a DESI-like BGS survey, provided the magnification bias is known to a few per cent, but only marginally, SNR $\lesssim2.5$, for the higher-redshift surveys, and not with the single-tracer bispectrum dipole.

title: Lagrangian transport driven by travelling waves in a radially deforming circular cavity
summary: A travelling deformation of a circular cavity wall can carry particles with the wave or against it. For two counter-propagating waves of azimuthal order $m$ and amplitudes $a$ and $b$, the leading axisymmetric component of the total (Lagrangian) drift scales with the intensity difference $S_3=|a|^2-|b|^2$. We obtain the radial profile of the azimuthal drift in closed form in the viscous limit, where the Womersley number $\mathrm{Wo}$ tends to zero, and by quadrature for any finite $\mathrm{Wo}>0$. The total drift is the sum of the Eulerian mean velocity and the Stokes drift. For radial wall motion with $m\ge2$ and unequal wave intensities, the total drift follows the stronger of the two waves throughout the interior in the viscous limit, although the Stokes drift changes sign with radius for all $\mathrm{Wo}$. For $m=2$ and large $\mathrm{Wo}$, the predicted total drift just inside a radially moving wall opposes the wave to leading order in wall amplitude. For the same travelling shape, the total drift there follows the wave when the wall material also moves tangentially to preserve local arc length to first order. For the radial wall at large $\mathrm{Wo}$, the near-wall profile consists of the planar Longuet-Higgins result and a closed-form curvature correction. At large $m$ the core rotation approaches Tuck's finite-Reynolds-number waving-sheet result. At $m=2$ and $\mathrm{Wo}^2=10$, moving-domain simulations recover the leading-order drift coefficients for both wall motions.

title: The Galaxy Activity, Torus, and Outflow Survey: N. Little Red Dots are not dust deficient: constraints from Seyfert 1 JWST spectra
summary: Little Red Dots (LRDs) are compact, red sources discovered by JWST. Most show broad permitted emission lines characteristic of AGN, but other properties differ from local AGN, such as X-ray and radio weakness and an apparent scarcity of dust. If LRDs at z>4 are indeed dust deficient, the bolometric luminosities and black hole (BH) masses measured from SED fitting would be overestimated, and their red optical continuum would be intrinsic rather than reddened. Here we use rest-frame 3-27 micron JWST spectra of a sample of nearby (D<60 Mpc) Seyfert 1 (Sy1) nuclei to place constraints on the dust emission of LRDs. We normalised the individual Sy1 spectra by their broad H$α$ and 5100 A continuum luminosities and stacked them, obtaining scalings that reproduce, within a factor of three, the rest-frame near-infrared emission of a NIRSpec+MIRI stack of 249 LRDs at 2.3<z<9.3 and the near- and mid-infrared emission of a local LRD at z=0.1, with the 5100 A continuum giving the more reliable prediction when modest extinction is considered (Av<1 mag). However, simultaneously reproducing the optical and infrared SEDs of LRDs requires a more reddened accretion disc (Av ~ 2 mag) and a torus with a lower reprocessing efficiency (Ct ~ 0.1-0.2) than inferred for local Sy1 galaxies. This combination offers an alternative to BH-star scenarios that explain the optical continuum as an unreddened blackbody of T ~ 5000 K. Our model, based on local Sy1s, yields a more plausible infrared-to-optical energy balance, suggesting that LRDs are not dust deficient. From the torus model that reproduces the optical and near-infrared SED of the high-redshift LRD stack, we estimate a dust mass of $M_{\rm dust}\simeq10^4\,M_\odot$, consistent with the dust masses typical of AGN tori.

title: Held While Waiting: What LLM Agent Sessions Reserve on Serverless and Agent Runtimes
summary:
LLM agents spend nearly all their time waiting for the model. On Amazon Bedrock AgentCore, our agents waited a median of 2.7 seconds for each model reply, then computed for an estimated 5 to 40 milliseconds. AgentCore does not charge for CPU during the wait.
